100: {

106:     {
107:       return;

114:       g_drag_start = p;

116:   else if (code == LV_EVENT_PRESSING)
117:     {
118:       if (g_drag_start.y - p.y > UNLOCK_DRAG_DIST)
119:         {
120:           launcher_unlock();
121:         }
122:     }
123:   else if (code == LV_EVENT_SHORT_CLICKED)
124:     {
125:       launcher_unlock();
126:     }

258: static void launcher_paint_dot(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t r)
259: {
260:   int32_t dx;
261:   int32_t dy;
262:   int32_t w = LAUNCHER_SCREEN_W;
263:   int32_t h = LAUNCHER_SCREEN_H;
264: 
265:   for (dy = -r; dy <= r; dy++)
266:     {
267:       for (dx = -r; dx <= r; dx++)
268:         {
269:           if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= r * r &&
270:               x + dx >= 0 && x + dx < w && y + dy >= 0 && y + dy < h)
271:             {
272:               g_canvas_buf[(y + dy) * w + (x + dx)] = g_brush_color;
273:             }
274:         }
275:     }
276: }
277: 
278: static void launcher_paint_stroke(int32_t x0, int32_t y0,
279:                                   int32_t x1, int32_t y1)
280: {
281:   int32_t dx = x1 - x0;
282:   int32_t dy = y1 - y0;
283:   int32_t steps = abs(dx) > abs(dy) ? abs(dx) : abs(dy);
284:   int32_t i;
285: 
286:   if (steps == 0)
287:     {
288:       launcher_paint_dot(x1, y1, 6);
289:       return;
290:     }
291: 
292:   for (i = 0; i <= steps; i += 4)
293:     {
294:       launcher_paint_dot(x0 + dx * i / steps, y0 + dy * i / steps, 6);
295:     }
296: }

298: static void launcher_canvas_event_cb(lv_event_t *e)

318:     {

320:       g_brush_prev = p;
321:     }

31:  *   GPIOA_0  I2C0 SDA (3.3V pull-up)
32:  *   GPIOA_1  I2C0 SCL (3.3V pull-up)
33:  *   GPIOA_9  touch reset, active low
34:  *   GPIOA_10 touch interrupt
35:  */
36: 
37: #define CTP_I2C_ADDR         0x5d
38: 
39: #define CTP_RST_PIN          9
40: #define CTP_INT_PIN          10
41: 
42: #define CTP_INT_GPIO         S6_GPIOA(CTP_INT_PIN)
43: #define CTP_INT_CHANNEL      0
44: 
45: #define CTP_IRQ              S6_GPIOINT_IRQ(CTP_INT_CHANNEL)
46: 
47: /* Reset timing from the Goodix GT911 datasheet / mainline goodix.c */
48: 
49: #define CTP_RST_HOLD_MS      20     /* T2: > 10ms with reset asserted     */
50: #define CTP_ADDR_SETUP_US    100    /* T3: > 100us INT level before reset */
51: #define CTP_RST_RELEASE_MS   10     /* T4: > 5ms after reset deasserted   */
52: #define CTP_INT_SYNC_MS      50     /* T5: INT low pulse after reset      */
53: 
54: /****************************************************************************
55:  * Private Function Prototypes
56:  ****************************************************************************/
57: 
58: static int gt9xx_irq_attach(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state,
59:                             xcpt_t isr, void *arg);
60: static void gt9xx_irq_enable(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state, bool enable);
61: static int gt9xx_set_power(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state, bool on);
62: 
63: /****************************************************************************
64:  * Private Data
65:  ****************************************************************************/
66: 
67: /* Callback for Board-Specific Operations */
68: 
69: static const struct gt9xx_board_s g_vsai_logicpi_a1_gt9xx =
70: {
71:   .irq_attach = gt9xx_irq_attach,
72:   .irq_enable = gt9xx_irq_enable,
73:   .set_power  = gt9xx_set_power
74: };
75: 
76: /****************************************************************************
77:  * Private Functions
78:  ****************************************************************************/
79: 
80: /****************************************************************************
81:  * Name: gt911_reset
82:  *
83:  * Description:
84:  *   Run the GT911 power-on reset sequence.  INT held low during reset
85:  *   selects the 0x5d I2C address.
86:  *
87:  ****************************************************************************/
88: 
89: static int gt911_reset(void)
90: {
91:   int ret;
92: 
93:   ret = s6_gpioa_config_output(CTP_RST_PIN, false);
94:   if (ret < 0)
95:     {
96:       return ret;
97:     }
98: 
99:   nxsig_usleep(CTP_RST_HOLD_MS * 1000);
100: 
101:   ret = s6_gpioa_config_output(CTP_INT_PIN, false);
102:   if (ret < 0)
103:     {
104:       return ret;
105:     }
106: 
107:   nxsig_usleep(CTP_ADDR_SETUP_US);
108: 
109:   s6_gpioa_write(CTP_RST_PIN, true);
110:   nxsig_usleep(CTP_RST_RELEASE_MS * 1000);
111: 
112:   nxsig_usleep(CTP_INT_SYNC_MS * 1000);
113: 
114:   return s6_gpioa_config_input(CTP_INT_PIN);
115: }
116: 
117: /****************************************************************************
118:  * Name: gt9xx_irq_attach
119:  *
120:  * Description:
121:  *   Attach the Touch Panel Interrupt Handler and arm the gpio_intc
122:  *   channel for a falling edge on GPIOA_10.
123:  *
124:  ****************************************************************************/
125: 
126: static int gt9xx_irq_attach(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state,
127:                             xcpt_t isr, void *arg)
128: {
129:   int ret;
130: 
131:   iinfo("\n");
132: 
133:   ret = irq_attach(CTP_IRQ, isr, arg);
134:   if (ret < 0)
135:     {
136:       ierr("irq_attach failed: %d\n", ret);
137:       return ret;
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* A GPIO edge is converted by gpio_intc into a rising-edge pulse for the
141:    * GIC.  This matches meson_gpio_irq_type_output() in the vendor SDK.
142:    */
143: 
144:   up_set_irq_type(CTP_IRQ, IRQ_RISING_EDGE);
145: 
146:   ret = s6_gpioint_config(CTP_INT_CHANNEL, CTP_INT_GPIO,
147:                           IRQ_FALLING_EDGE);
148:   if (ret < 0)
149:     {
150:       irq_detach(CTP_IRQ);
151:     }
152: 
153:   return ret;
154: }
155: 
156: /****************************************************************************
157:  * Name: gt9xx_irq_enable
158:  *
159:  * Description:
160:  *   Enable or disable Touch Panel Interrupts at the GIC.
161:  *
162:  ****************************************************************************/
163: 
164: static void gt9xx_irq_enable(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state, bool enable)
165: {
166:   iinfo("enable=%d\n", enable);
167: 
168:   if (enable)
169:     {
170:       up_enable_irq(CTP_IRQ);
171:     }
172:   else
173:     {
174:       up_disable_irq(CTP_IRQ);
175:     }
176: }
177: 
178: /****************************************************************************
179:  * Name: gt9xx_set_power
180:  *
181:  * Description:
182:  *   Power the Touch Panel up with the GT911 reset sequence, or leave it
183:  *   running on close (holding reset would stop touch scanning).
184:  *
185:  ****************************************************************************/
186: 
187: static int gt9xx_set_power(const struct gt9xx_board_s *state, bool on)
188: {
189:   iinfo("on=%d\n", on);
190: 
191:   return on ? gt911_reset() : OK;
192: }
193: 
194: /****************************************************************************
195:  * Public Functions
196:  ****************************************************************************/
197: 
198: /****************************************************************************
199:  * Name: vsai_logicpi_a1_touch_register
200:  *
201:  * Description:
202:  *   Register the GT911 Touch Panel on I2C0 as devpath (e.g. "/dev/input0").
203:  *
204:  * Input Parameters:
205:  *   devpath - Device Path (e.g. "/dev/input0")
206:  *   i2c     - I2C bus (as returned by s6_i2cbus_initialize())
207:  *
208:  * Returned Value:
209:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
210:  *
211:  ****************************************************************************/
212: 
213: int vsai_logicpi_a1_touch_register(FAR const char *devpath,
214:                                    FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c)
215: {
216:   int ret;
217: 
218:   iinfo("devpath=%s\n", devpath);
219: 
220:   /* Route I2C0 to GPIOA_0 (SDA) / GPIOA_1 (SCL), function 3 */
221: 
222:   ret = s6_gpioa_set_mux(0, 3);
223:   if (ret < 0)
224:     {
225:       ierr("SDA mux failed: %d\n", ret);
226:       return ret;
227:     }
228: 
229:   ret = s6_gpioa_set_mux(1, 3);
230:   if (ret < 0)
231:     {
232:       ierr("SCL mux failed: %d\n", ret);
233:       return ret;
234:     }
235: 
236:   ret = gt9xx_register(devpath, i2c, CTP_I2C_ADDR, &g_vsai_logicpi_a1_gt9xx);
237:   if (ret < 0)
238:     {
239:       ierr("gt9xx_register failed: %d\n", ret);
240:     }
241: 
242:   return ret;
243: }

1: # launcher（LVGL 演示）
2: 
3: 队伍 349 FedoraVForce 的 LVGL 触控演示应用，映射到 openvela
4: `packages/demos/contest2026_349_launcher`。
5: 
6: - 锁屏页：运行时钟，上滑/点击圆形手柄解锁
7: - 桌面页：时钟、heap/FPS 状态、About / Paint 两个入口
8: - About 页：S6 移植信息（GICv3、MIPI DSI、GT9XX）与实时 heap/FPS

10: 
11: 运行：NSH 下执行 `launcher`。

72: lv_indev_t * lv_nuttx_touchscreen_create(const char * dev_path)
73: {
74:     lv_indev_t * indev;
75:     uint8_t maxpoint;
76:     int fd;
77: 
78:     LV_ASSERT_NULL(dev_path);
79:     LV_LOG_USER("touchscreen %s opening", dev_path);
80:     fd = open(dev_path, O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC);
81:     if(fd < 0) {
82:         LV_LOG_ERROR("cannot open touchscreen device %s, (errno=%d)", dev_path, errno);
83:         return NULL;
84:     }
85: 
86:     if(ioctl(fd, TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS, &maxpoint) < 0) {
87:         LV_LOG_ERROR("get touch maxpoints failed (errno=%d)", errno);
88:         close(fd);
89:         return NULL;
90:     }
91: 
92:     if(maxpoint == 0) {
93:         LV_LOG_ERROR("touchscreen %s unsupported maxpoint %d", dev_path, maxpoint);
94:         close(fd);
95:         return NULL;
96:     }
97: 
98:     LV_LOG_USER("touchscreen %s open success, maxpoint %d", dev_path, maxpoint);
99: 
100:     indev = touchscreen_init(fd, maxpoint);
101: 
102:     if(indev == NULL) {
103:         close(fd);
104:         return NULL;
105:     }
106: 
107:     indev_set_cursor(indev, LV_NUTTX_TOUCHSCREEN_CURSOR_SIZE);
108: 
109:     return indev;
110: }

116: static void indev_set_cursor(lv_indev_t * indev, int32_t size)
117: {
118:     lv_obj_t * cursor_obj = lv_indev_get_cursor(indev);
119:     if(size <= 0) {
120:         if(cursor_obj) {
121:             lv_obj_delete(cursor_obj);
122:             lv_indev_set_cursor(indev, NULL);
123:         }
124:     }
125:     else {
126:         if(cursor_obj == NULL) {
127:             cursor_obj = lv_obj_create(lv_layer_sys());
128:             lv_obj_remove_style_all(cursor_obj);
129:             lv_obj_set_style_radius(cursor_obj, LV_RADIUS_CIRCLE, 0);
130:             lv_obj_set_style_bg_opa(cursor_obj, LV_OPA_50, 0);
131:             lv_obj_set_style_bg_color(cursor_obj, lv_color_black(), 0);
132:             lv_obj_set_style_border_width(cursor_obj, 2, 0);
133:             lv_obj_set_style_border_color(cursor_obj, lv_palette_main(LV_PALETTE_GREY), 0);
134:         }
135:         lv_obj_set_size(cursor_obj, size, size);
136:         lv_obj_set_style_translate_x(cursor_obj, -size / 2, 0);
137:         lv_obj_set_style_translate_y(cursor_obj, -size / 2, 0);
138:         lv_indev_set_cursor(indev, cursor_obj);
139:     }
140: }

142: static void process_single_touch(lv_indev_t * drv,
143:                                  lv_indev_data_t * data,
144:                                  struct touch_sample_s * sample)
145: {
146:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = drv->driver_data;
147:     uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[0].flags;
148: 
149:     if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
150:         lv_display_t * disp = lv_indev_get_display(drv);
151:         int32_t hor_max = lv_display_get_horizontal_resolution(disp) - 1;
152:         int32_t ver_max = lv_display_get_vertical_resolution(disp) - 1;
153: 
154:         data->point.x = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[0].x, hor_max);
155:         data->point.y = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[0].y, ver_max);
156:         touchscreen->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
157: 
158:         if(touch_flags & TOUCH_DOWN) {
159:             touchscreen->primary_point.id = sample->point[0].id;
160:             touchscreen->primary_point.x = data->point.x;
161:             touchscreen->primary_point.y = data->point.y;
162:         }
163:     }
164:     else if(touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) {
165:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
166:         touchscreen->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
167:     }
168: }

170: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
171: static void touchscreen_update_primary_point(struct touch_sample_s * sample,
172:                                              lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen,
173:                                              int32_t hor_max, int32_t ver_max)
174: {
175:     int primary_index = -1;
176: 
177:     for(int i = 0; i < sample->npoints; i++) {
178:         uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[i].flags;
179: 
180:         if(touchscreen->primary_point.id == sample->point[i].id) {
181:             if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
182:                 primary_index = i;
183:                 break;
184:             }
185:             else if((touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) && primary_index >= 0) {
186:                 break;
187:             }
188:         }
189:         else if((touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) && primary_index < 0) {
190:             primary_index = i;
191:         }
192:     }
193: 
194:     if(primary_index != -1) {
195:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = sample->point[primary_index].id;
196:         touchscreen->primary_point.x =
197:             LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[primary_index].x, hor_max);
198:         touchscreen->primary_point.y =
199:             LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[primary_index].y, ver_max);
200:     }
201:     else {
202:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
203:     }
204: }

206: static void process_multi_touch(lv_indev_t * indev,
207:                                 lv_indev_data_t * data,
208:                                 struct touch_sample_s * sample)
209: {
210:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = lv_indev_get_driver_data(indev);
211:     lv_indev_touch_data_t * touch_data_tmp = touchscreen->touch_data;
212:     lv_display_t * disp = lv_indev_get_display(indev);
213:     int32_t hor_max = lv_display_get_horizontal_resolution(disp) - 1;
214:     int32_t ver_max = lv_display_get_vertical_resolution(disp) - 1;
215:     uint16_t finger_release_cnt = 0;
216: 
217:     for(int i = 0; i < sample->npoints; i++) {
218:         touch_data_tmp->id = sample->point[i].id;
219:         uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[i].flags;
220:         if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
221:             touch_data_tmp->point.x = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[i].x, hor_max);
222:             touch_data_tmp->point.y = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[i].y, ver_max);
223:             touch_data_tmp->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
224:             touch_data_tmp++;
225:         }
226:         else if(touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) {
227:             touch_data_tmp->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
228:             finger_release_cnt++;
229:             touch_data_tmp++;
230:         }
231:     }
232: 
233:     lv_indev_gesture_detect_pinch(&touchscreen->recognizer,
234:                                   touchscreen->touch_data,
235:                                   touchscreen->active_points);
236:     lv_indev_set_gesture_data(data, &touchscreen->recognizer);
237: 
238:     data->update_primary_point = false;
239:     if(finger_release_cnt == touchscreen->active_points) {
240:         data->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
241:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
242:     }
243:     else {
244:         data->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
245:         if(finger_release_cnt > 0) {
246:             data->update_primary_point = true;
247:         }
248: 
249:         touchscreen_update_primary_point(sample, touchscreen, hor_max, ver_max);
250:         data->point.x = touchscreen->primary_point.x;
251:         data->point.y = touchscreen->primary_point.y;
252:     }
253: }
254: #endif
255: 
256: static void conv_touch(lv_indev_t * drv,
257:                        lv_indev_data_t * data,
258:                        struct touch_sample_s * sample)
259: {
260: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
261:     if(sample->npoints > 1) {
262:         lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = drv->driver_data;
263:         touchscreen->active_points = 0;
264: 
265:         for(int i = 0; i < sample->npoints; i++) {
266:             if((sample->point[i].flags)) {
267:                 ++touchscreen->active_points;
268:             }
269:         }
270: 
271:         if(touchscreen->active_points > 1) {
272:             process_multi_touch(drv, data, sample);
273:             return;
274:         }
275:     }
276: 
277: #endif
278:     process_single_touch(drv, data, sample);
279: }
280: static bool touchscreen_read_sample(lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen)
281: {
282:     int nbytes = read(touchscreen->fd,
283:                       touchscreen->sample,
284:                       SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(touchscreen->maxpoint));
285:     return nbytes == SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(touchscreen->maxpoint);
286: }
287: 
288: static void touchscreen_read(lv_indev_t * drv, lv_indev_data_t * data)
289: {
290:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = drv->driver_data;
291: 
292:     /* Note: Since it is necessary to avoid multi-processing click events
293:     * caused by redundant continue_reading, a two-unit sample sliding window
294:     * algorithm is used here. continue_reading is only activated when there
295:     * are two points in the window.
296:     */
297: 
298:     /* If has last sample, use it first */
299:     if(touchscreen->has_last_sample) {
300:         conv_touch(drv, data, touchscreen->last_sample);
301:     }
302:     else {
303:         /* Read first sample */
304:         if(!touchscreen_read_sample(touchscreen)) {
305:             /* No sample available, return last state */
306: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
307:             if(touchscreen->active_points > 1) {
308:                 return;
309:             }
310: #endif
311:             data->state = touchscreen->last_state;
312:             return;
313:         }
314: 
315:         conv_touch(drv, data, touchscreen->sample);
316:     }
317: 
318:     /* Try to read next sample */
319:     if(touchscreen_read_sample(touchscreen)) {
320:         /* Save last sample and let lvgl continue reading */
321:         lv_memcpy(touchscreen->last_sample, touchscreen->sample,
322:                   SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(touchscreen->maxpoint));
323:         touchscreen->has_last_sample = true;
324:         data->continue_reading = true;
325:     }
326:     else {
327:         /* No more sample available, clear last sample flag */
328:         touchscreen->has_last_sample = false;
329:     }
330: 
331: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
332:     if(touchscreen->active_points > 1) {
333:         return;
334:     }
335: #endif
336:     data->state = touchscreen->last_state;
337: }
338: 
339: static void touchscreen_delete_cb(lv_event_t * e)
340: {
341:     lv_indev_t * indev = (lv_indev_t *) lv_event_get_user_data(e);
342:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = lv_indev_get_driver_data(indev);
343:     if(touchscreen) {
344:         if(touchscreen->sample) {
345:             lv_free(touchscreen->sample);
346:             touchscreen->sample = NULL;
347:         }
348: 
349:         if(touchscreen->last_sample) {
350:             lv_free(touchscreen->last_sample);
351:             touchscreen->last_sample = NULL;
352:         }
353: 
354: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
355:         if(touchscreen->touch_data) {
356:             lv_free(touchscreen->touch_data);
357:             touchscreen->touch_data = NULL;
358:         }
359: #endif
360: 
361:         lv_indev_set_driver_data(indev, NULL);
362:         lv_indev_set_read_cb(indev, NULL);
363:         indev_set_cursor(indev, -1);
364:         if(touchscreen->fd >= 0) {
365:             close(touchscreen->fd);
366:             touchscreen->fd = -1;
367:         }
368:         lv_free(touchscreen);
369:         LV_LOG_USER("done");
370:     }
371: }
372: 
373: static lv_indev_t * touchscreen_init(int fd, uint8_t maxpoint)
374: {
375:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen;
376:     lv_indev_t * indev = NULL;
377: 
378:     touchscreen = lv_malloc_zeroed(sizeof(lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t));
379:     if(touchscreen == NULL) {
380:         LV_LOG_ERROR("touchscreen_s malloc failed");
381:         return NULL;
382:     }
383: 
384:     touchscreen->fd = fd;
385:     touchscreen->maxpoint = maxpoint;
386:     touchscreen->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
387:     touchscreen->indev_drv = indev = lv_indev_create();
388:     touchscreen->sample =
389:         lv_malloc_zeroed(SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(touchscreen->maxpoint));
390:     LV_ASSERT_MALLOC(touchscreen->sample);
391: 
392:     touchscreen->last_sample =
393:         lv_malloc_zeroed(SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(touchscreen->maxpoint));
394:     LV_ASSERT_MALLOC(touchscreen->last_sample);
395: 
396: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
397:     touchscreen->touch_data =
398:         lv_malloc_zeroed(sizeof(lv_indev_touch_data_t) * touchscreen->maxpoint);
399:     LV_ASSERT_MALLOC(touchscreen->touch_data);
400: #endif
401: 
402:     lv_indev_set_type(indev, LV_INDEV_TYPE_POINTER);
403:     lv_indev_set_read_cb(indev, touchscreen_read);
404:     lv_indev_set_driver_data(indev, touchscreen);
405:     lv_indev_add_event_cb(indev, touchscreen_delete_cb, LV_EVENT_DELETE, indev);
406:     return indev;
407: }

78:     if(disp == NULL) {
79:         lv_free(dsc);
80:         return NULL;
81:     }
82:     dsc->fd = -1;
83:     lv_display_set_driver_data(disp, dsc);
84:     lv_display_add_event_cb(disp, display_release_cb, LV_EVENT_DELETE, disp);
85:     lv_display_set_flush_cb(disp, flush_cb);
86:     return disp;

89: int lv_nuttx_fbdev_set_file(lv_display_t * disp, const char * file)
90: {
91:     int ret;
92:     LV_ASSERT(disp && file);
93:     lv_nuttx_fb_t * dsc = lv_display_get_driver_data(disp);
94: 
95:     if(dsc->fd >= 0) close(dsc->fd);
96: 
97:     /* Open the file for reading and writing*/
98: 
99:     dsc->fd = open(file, O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
100:     if(dsc->fd < 0) {
101:         LV_LOG_ERROR("Error: cannot open framebuffer device");
102:         return -errno;
103:     }
104:     LV_LOG_USER("The framebuffer device was opened successfully");
105: 
106:     if(ioctl(dsc->fd, FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO, (unsigned long)((uintptr_t)&dsc->vinfo)) < 0) {
107:         LV_LOG_ERROR("ioctl(FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO) failed: %d", errno);
108:         ret = -errno;
109:         goto errout;
110:     }
111: 
112:     LV_LOG_USER("VideoInfo:");
113:     LV_LOG_USER("      fmt: %u", dsc->vinfo.fmt);
114:     LV_LOG_USER("     xres: %u", dsc->vinfo.xres);
115:     LV_LOG_USER("     yres: %u", dsc->vinfo.yres);
116:     LV_LOG_USER("  nplanes: %u", dsc->vinfo.nplanes);
117: 
118:     if((ret = fbdev_get_pinfo(dsc->fd, &dsc->pinfo)) < 0) {
119:         goto errout;
120:     }
121: 
122:     lv_color_format_t color_format = fb_fmt_to_color_format(dsc->vinfo.fmt);
123:     if(color_format == LV_COLOR_FORMAT_UNKNOWN) {
124:         goto errout;
125:     }
126: 
127:     dsc->mem = mmap(NULL, dsc->pinfo.fblen, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
128:                     MAP_SHARED | MAP_FILE, dsc->fd, 0);
129:     if(dsc->mem == MAP_FAILED) {
130:         LV_LOG_ERROR("ioctl(FBIOGET_PLANEINFO) failed: %d", errno);
131:         ret = -errno;
132:         goto errout;
133:     }
134: 
135:     uint32_t w = dsc->vinfo.xres;
136:     uint32_t h = dsc->vinfo.yres;
137:     uint32_t stride = dsc->pinfo.stride;
138:     uint32_t data_size = h * stride;
139:     lv_draw_buf_init(&dsc->buf1, w, h, color_format, stride, dsc->mem, data_size);
140: 
141:     /* double buffer mode */
142: 
143:     bool double_buffer = dsc->pinfo.yres_virtual == (dsc->vinfo.yres * 2);
144:     if(double_buffer) {
145:         if((ret = fbdev_init_mem2(dsc)) < 0) {
146:             goto errout;
147:         }
148: 
149:         lv_draw_buf_init(&dsc->buf2, w, h, color_format, stride, dsc->mem2, data_size);
150:     }
151: 
152:     lv_display_set_draw_buffers(disp, &dsc->buf1, double_buffer ? &dsc->buf2 : NULL);
153:     lv_display_set_color_format(disp, color_format);
154:     lv_display_set_render_mode(disp, LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_DIRECT);
155:     lv_display_set_resolution(disp, dsc->vinfo.xres, dsc->vinfo.yres);
156:     lv_timer_set_cb(disp->refr_timer, display_refr_timer_cb);
157: 
158: #if LV_DRAW_TRANSFORM_USE_MATRIX
159:     lv_display_set_matrix_rotation(disp, true);
160: #endif
161: 
162:     LV_LOG_USER("Resolution is set to %dx%d at %" LV_PRId32 "dpi",
163:                 dsc->vinfo.xres, dsc->vinfo.yres, lv_display_get_dpi(disp));
164:     return 0;
165: 
166: errout:
167:     close(dsc->fd);
168:     dsc->fd = -1;
169:     return ret;
170: }

176: static void display_refr_timer_cb(lv_timer_t * tmr)
177: {
178:     lv_display_t * disp = lv_timer_get_user_data(tmr);
179:     lv_nuttx_fb_t * dsc = lv_display_get_driver_data(disp);
180:     struct pollfd pfds[1];
181: 
182:     lv_memzero(pfds, sizeof(pfds));
183:     pfds[0].fd = dsc->fd;
184:     pfds[0].events = POLLOUT;
185: 
186:     /* Query free fb to draw */
187: 
188:     if(poll(pfds, 1, 0) < 0) {
189:         return;
190:     }
191: 
192:     if(pfds[0].revents & POLLOUT) {
193:         _lv_display_refr_timer(tmr);
194:     }
195: }

197: static void flush_cb(lv_display_t * disp, const lv_area_t * area, uint8_t * color_p)
198: {
199:     lv_nuttx_fb_t * dsc = lv_display_get_driver_data(disp);
200: 
201:     /* Skip the non-last flush */
202: 
203:     if(!lv_display_flush_is_last(disp)) {
204:         lv_display_flush_ready(disp);
205:         return;
206:     }
207: 
208:     if(dsc->mem == NULL ||
209:        area->x2 < 0 || area->y2 < 0 ||
210:        area->x1 > (int32_t)dsc->vinfo.xres - 1 || area->y1 > (int32_t)dsc->vinfo.yres - 1) {
211:         lv_display_flush_ready(disp);
212:         return;
213:     }
214: 
215: #if defined(CONFIG_FB_UPDATE)
216:     /*May be some direct update command is required*/
217:     int yoffset = disp->buf_act == disp->buf_1 ?
218:                   0 : dsc->mem2_yoffset;
219: 
220:     /* Join the areas to update */
221:     lv_area_t dirty_area;
222:     lv_display_get_dirty_area(disp, &dirty_area);
223: 
224:     struct fb_area_s fb_area;
225:     fb_area.x = dirty_area.x1;
226:     fb_area.y = dirty_area.y1 + yoffset;
227:     fb_area.w = lv_area_get_width(&dirty_area);
228:     fb_area.h = lv_area_get_height(&dirty_area);
229:     if(ioctl(dsc->fd, FBIO_UPDATE, (unsigned long)((uintptr_t)&fb_area)) < 0) {
230:         LV_LOG_ERROR("ioctl(FBIO_UPDATE) failed: %d", errno);
231:     }
232: #endif
233: 
234:     /* double framebuffer */
235: 
236:     if(dsc->mem2 != NULL) {
237:         if(disp->buf_act == disp->buf_1) {
238:             dsc->pinfo.yoffset = 0;
239:         }
240:         else {
241:             dsc->pinfo.yoffset = dsc->mem2_yoffset;
242:         }
243: 
244:         if(ioctl(dsc->fd, FBIOPAN_DISPLAY, (unsigned long)((uintptr_t) & (dsc->pinfo))) < 0) {
245:             LV_LOG_ERROR("ioctl(FBIOPAN_DISPLAY) failed: %d", errno);
246:         }
247:     }
248:     lv_display_flush_ready(disp);
249: }

251: static lv_color_format_t fb_fmt_to_color_format(int fmt)
252: {
253:     switch(fmt) {
254:         case FB_FMT_RGB16_565:
255:             return LV_COLOR_FORMAT_RGB565;
256:         case FB_FMT_RGB24:
257:             return LV_COLOR_FORMAT_RGB888;
258:         case FB_FMT_RGB32:
259:             return LV_COLOR_FORMAT_XRGB8888;
260:         case FB_FMT_RGBA32:
261:             return LV_COLOR_FORMAT_ARGB8888;
262:         default:
263:             break;
264:     }
265: 
266:     LV_LOG_ERROR("Unsupported color format: %d", fmt);
267: 
268:     return LV_COLOR_FORMAT_UNKNOWN;
269: }

271: static int fbdev_get_pinfo(int fd, FAR struct fb_planeinfo_s * pinfo)
272: {
273:     if(ioctl(fd, FBIOGET_PLANEINFO, (unsigned long)((uintptr_t)pinfo)) < 0) {
274:         LV_LOG_ERROR("ERROR: ioctl(FBIOGET_PLANEINFO) failed: %d", errno);
275:         return -errno;
276:     }
277: 
278:     LV_LOG_USER("PlaneInfo (plane %d):", pinfo->display);
279:     LV_LOG_USER("    mem: %p", pinfo->fbmem);
280:     LV_LOG_USER("    fblen: %zu", pinfo->fblen);
281:     LV_LOG_USER("   stride: %u", pinfo->stride);
282:     LV_LOG_USER("  display: %u", pinfo->display);
283:     LV_LOG_USER("      bpp: %u", pinfo->bpp);
284: 
285:     return 0;
286: }
287: 
288: static int fbdev_init_mem2(lv_nuttx_fb_t * dsc)
289: {
290:     struct fb_planeinfo_s pinfo;
291:     void * phy_mem1;
292:     void * phy_mem2;
293: 
294:     int ret;
295: 
296:     /* Get display[0] planeinfo */
297:     lv_memzero(&pinfo, sizeof(pinfo));
298:     pinfo.display = dsc->pinfo.display;
299:     if((ret = fbdev_get_pinfo(dsc->fd, &pinfo)) < 0) return ret;
300:     phy_mem1 = pinfo.fbmem;
301: 
302:     /* Get display[1] planeinfo */
303:     lv_memzero(&pinfo, sizeof(pinfo));
304:     pinfo.display = dsc->pinfo.display + 1;
305:     if((ret = fbdev_get_pinfo(dsc->fd, &pinfo)) < 0) return ret;
306:     phy_mem2 = pinfo.fbmem;
307: 
308:     lv_uintptr_t offset = (lv_uintptr_t)phy_mem2 - (lv_uintptr_t)phy_mem1;
309:     bool is_consecutive = offset == 0;
310: 
311:     /* Check bpp */
312: 
313:     if(pinfo.bpp != dsc->pinfo.bpp) {
314:         LV_LOG_WARN("mem2 is incorrect");
315:         return -EINVAL;
316:     }
317: 
318:     /* Check the buffer address offset,
319:      * It needs to be divisible by pinfo.stride
320:      */
321: 
322:     if((offset % dsc->pinfo.stride) != 0) {
323:         LV_LOG_WARN("It is detected that buf_offset(%" PRIuPTR ") "
324:                     "and stride(%d) are not divisible, please ensure "
325:                     "that the driver handles the address offset by itself.",
326:                     offset, dsc->pinfo.stride);
327:     }
328: 
329:     /* Calculate the address and yoffset of mem2 */
330: 
331:     if(is_consecutive) {
332:         dsc->mem2_yoffset = dsc->vinfo.yres;
333:         offset = dsc->vinfo.yres * pinfo.stride;
334:     }
335:     else {
336:         dsc->mem2_yoffset = offset / dsc->pinfo.stride;
337:     }
338: 
339:     uint32_t fblen = is_consecutive ? pinfo.fblen / 2 : pinfo.fblen;
340:     void * mem2 = mmap(NULL, fblen, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED | MAP_FILE, dsc->fd, offset);
341:     if(mem2 == MAP_FAILED) {
342:         LV_LOG_ERROR("ERROR: mmap failed: %d, offset: %" PRIuPTR, errno, offset);
343:         return -errno;
344:     }
345:     dsc->mem2 = mem2;
346: 
347:     LV_LOG_USER("Use of %sconsecutive mem2 = %p, yoffset = %" LV_PRIu32, is_consecutive ? "" : "non-", dsc->mem2,
348:                 dsc->mem2_yoffset);
349: 
350:     return 0;
351: }
352: 
353: static void display_release_cb(lv_event_t * e)
354: {
355:     lv_display_t * disp = (lv_display_t *) lv_event_get_user_data(e);
356:     lv_nuttx_fb_t * dsc = lv_display_get_driver_data(disp);
357:     if(dsc) {
358:         lv_display_set_driver_data(disp, NULL);
359:         lv_display_set_flush_cb(disp, NULL);
360: 
361:         if(dsc->mem != NULL && dsc->mem != MAP_FAILED) {
362:             /* Unmap the framebuffer memory */
363:             munmap(dsc->mem, dsc->pinfo.fblen);
364:             dsc->mem = NULL;
365:         }
366: 
367:         if(dsc->mem2 != NULL && dsc->mem2 != MAP_FAILED) {
368:             /* Unmap the second framebuffer memory if double buffering is used */
369:             munmap(dsc->mem2, dsc->pinfo.fblen);
370:             dsc->mem2 = NULL;
371:         }
372: 
373:         if(dsc->fd >= 0) {
374:             close(dsc->fd);
375:             dsc->fd = -1;
376:         }
377:         lv_free(dsc);
378:     }
379:     LV_LOG_USER("Done");
380: }

382: #endif /*LV_USE_NUTTX*/

158:  ****************************************************************************/
159: 
160: static int gt9xx_i2c_read(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
161:                           uint16_t reg,
162:                           uint8_t *buf,
163:                           size_t buflen)
164: {
165:   int ret;
166: 
167:   /* Send the Register Address, MSB first */
168: 
169:   uint8_t regbuf[2] =
170:   {
171:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
172:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
173:   };
174: 
175:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
176: 
177:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
178:   {
179:     {
180:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
181: 
182:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
183:       .addr      = dev->addr,
184:       .flags     = 0,
185:       .buffer    = regbuf,
186:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
187:     },
188:     {
189:       /* Receive the I2C Register Values */
190: 
191:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
192:       .addr      = dev->addr,
193:       .flags     = I2C_M_READ,
194:       .buffer    = buf,
195:       .length    = buflen
196:     }
197:   };
198: 
199:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
200: 
201:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, buflen=%ld\n", reg, buflen);
202:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c && buf);
203: 
204:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
205: 
206:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
207:   if (ret < 0)
208:     {
209:       ierr("I2C Read failed: %d\n", ret);
210:       return ret;
211:     }
212: 
213: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO
214:   iinfodumpbuffer("gt9xx_i2c_read", buf, buflen);
215: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO */
216: 
217:   return OK;
218: }

369: /****************************************************************************
370:  * Name: gt9xx_read_touch_data
371:  *
372:  * Description:
373:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
374:  *   Touch Points.
375:  *
376:  * Input Parameters:
377:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
378:  *   sample - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
379:  *
380:  * Returned Value:
381:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
382:  *
383:  ****************************************************************************/
384: 
385: static int gt9xx_read_touch_data(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
386:                                  FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample)
387: {
388:   uint8_t status[1];
389:   uint8_t status_code;
390:   uint8_t touched_points;
391:   uint8_t touch[6];
392:   uint16_t x;
393:   uint16_t y;
394:   uint8_t flags;
395:   int ret;
396: 
397:   /* Erase the Touch Sample and Touch Point */
398: 
399:   iinfo("\n");
400:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && sample);
401:   memset(sample, 0, sizeof(*sample));
402: 
403:   /* Read the Touch Panel Status */
404: 
405:   ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_READ_COOR_ADDR, status, sizeof(status));
406:   if (ret < 0)
407:     {
408:       ierr("Read Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
409:       return ret;
410:     }
411: 
412:   /* Decode the Status Code and the Touched Points */
413: 
414:   status_code = status[0] & 0x80;
415:   touched_points = status[0] & 0x0f;
416: 
417:   /* If Touch Panel Status is OK and Touched Points is 1 or more */
418: 
419:   if (status_code != 0 && touched_points >= 1)
420:     {
421:       /* Read the First Touch Point (6 bytes) */
422: 
423:       ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_POINT1, touch, sizeof(touch));
424:       if (ret < 0)
425:         {
426:           ierr("Read Touch Point failed: %d\n", ret);
427:           return ret;
428:         }
429: 
430:       /* Decode the Touch Coordinates */
431: 
432:       x = touch[0] + (touch[1] << 8);
433:       y = touch[2] + (touch[3] << 8);
434: 
435:       /* Return the Touch Coordinates as Touch Down */
436: 
437:       flags = TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
438:       sample->npoints = 1;
439:       sample->point[0].id = 0;
440:       sample->point[0].x = x;
441:       sample->point[0].y = y;
442:       sample->point[0].flags = flags;
443:       iinfo("touch down x=%d, y=%d\n", x, y);
444:     }
445: 
446:   /* Set the Touch Panel Status to 0 */
447: 
448:   ret = gt9xx_set_status(dev, 0);
449:   if (ret < 0)
450:     {
451:       ierr("Set Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
452:       return ret;
453:     }
454: 
455:   return OK;
456: }

458: /****************************************************************************
459:  * Name: gt9xx_read
460:  *
461:  * Description:
462:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
463:  *   Touch Points.
464:  *
465:  * Input Parameters:
466:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
467:  *   buffer - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
468:  *   buflen - Size of buffer
469:  *
470:  * Returned Value:
471:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
472:  *
473:  ****************************************************************************/
474: 
475: static ssize_t gt9xx_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
476:                           size_t buflen)
477: {
478:   FAR struct inode *inode;
479:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
480:   struct touch_sample_s sample;
481:   const size_t outlen = sizeof(sample);
482:   irqstate_t flags;
483:   int ret;
484: 
485:   /* Returned Touch Sample will have 0 or 1 Touch Points */
486: 
487:   iinfo("buflen=%ld\n", buflen);
488:   if (buflen < outlen)
489:     {
490:       ierr("Buffer should be at least %ld bytes, got %ld bytes\n",
491:            outlen, buflen);
492:       return -EINVAL;
493:     }
494: 
495:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
496: 
497:   inode = filep->f_inode;
498:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
499:   priv = inode->i_private;
500: 
501:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent reads */
502: 
503:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
504:   if (ret < 0)
505:     {
506:       return ret;
507:     }
508: 
509:   ret = -EINVAL;
510: 
511:   /* If waiting for Touch Up, return the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
512: 
513:   if (priv->flags & TOUCH_DOWN)
514:     {
515:       /* Begin Critical Section */
516: 
517:       flags = enter_critical_section();
518: 
519:       /* Mark the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
520: 
521:       priv->flags = TOUCH_UP | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
522: 
523:       /* End Critical Section */
524: 
525:       leave_critical_section(flags);
526: 
527:       /* Return the Last Touch Point, changed to Touch Up */
528: 
529:       memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
530:       sample.npoints = 1;
531:       sample.point[0].id = 0;
532:       sample.point[0].x = priv->x;
533:       sample.point[0].y = priv->y;
534:       sample.point[0].flags = priv->flags;
535:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
536:       ret = OK;
537:       iinfo("touch up x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
538:     }
539:   else
540:     {
541:       /* Otherwise read the Touch Point over I2C */
542: 
543:       ret = gt9xx_read_touch_data(priv, &sample);
544: 
545:       /* Skip duplicates */
546: 
547:       if (sample.npoints >= 1 &&
548:           priv->x == sample.point[0].x &&
549:           priv->y == sample.point[0].y)
550:         {
551:           memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
552:           sample.npoints = 0;
553:           iinfo("skip duplicate x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
554:         }
555: 
556:       /* Return the Touch Point */
557: 
558:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
559: 
560:       /* Begin Critical Section */
561: 
562:       flags = enter_critical_section();
563: 
564:       /* Clear the Interrupt Pending Flag */
565: 
566:       priv->int_pending = false;
567: 
568:       /* Remember the Last Touch Point */
569: 
570:       if (sample.npoints >= 1)
571:         {
572:           priv->x = sample.point[0].x;
573:           priv->y = sample.point[0].y;
574:           priv->flags = sample.point[0].flags;
575:         }
576: 
577:       /* End Critical Section */
578: 
579:       leave_critical_section(flags);
580:     }
581: 
582:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow next read */
583: 
584:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
585:   return (ret < 0) ? ret : outlen;
586: }

588: /****************************************************************************
589:  * Name: gt9xx_open
590:  *
591:  * Description:
592:  *   Open the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the first open, we power on
593:  *   the Touch Panel, probe for the Touch Panel and enable Touch Panel
594:  *   Interrupts.
595:  *
596:  * Input Parameters:
597:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
598:  *
599:  * Returned Value:
600:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
601:  *
602:  ****************************************************************************/
603: 
604: static int gt9xx_open(FAR struct file *filep)
605: {
606:   FAR struct inode *inode;
607:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
608:   unsigned int use_count;
609:   int ret;
610: 
611:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
612: 
613:   iinfo("\n");
614:   inode = filep->f_inode;
615:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
616:   priv = inode->i_private;
617: 
618:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
619: 
620:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
621:   if (ret < 0)
622:     {
623:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
624:       return ret;
625:     }
626: 
627:   /* Get next Reference Count */
628: 
629:   use_count = priv->cref + 1;
630:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count < UINT8_MAX && use_count > priv->cref);
631:   if (use_count == 1)
632:     {
633:       /* If first user, power on the Touch Panel */
634: 
635:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power != NULL);
636:       ret = priv->board->set_power(priv->board, true);
637:       if (ret < 0)
638:         {
639:           goto out_lock;
640:         }
641: 
642:       /* Let Touch Panel power up before probing */
643: 
644:       nxsig_usleep(100 * 1000);
645: 
646:       /* Check that Touch Panel exists on I2C */
647: 
648:       ret = gt9xx_probe_device(priv);
649:       if (ret < 0)
650:         {
651:           /* No such device, power off the Touch Panel */
652: 
653:           priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
654:           goto out_lock;
655:         }
656: 
657:       /* Enable Touch Panel Interrupts */
658: 
659:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
660:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, true);
661:     }
662: 
663:   /* Set the Reference Count */
664: 
665:   priv->cref = use_count;
666: 
667:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
668: 
669: out_lock:
670:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
671:   return ret;
672: }
673: 
674: /****************************************************************************
675:  * Name: gt9xx_close
676:  *
677:  * Description:
678:  *   Close the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the final close, we disable
679:  *   Touch Panel Interrupts and power off the Touch Panel.
680:  *
681:  * Input Parameters:
682:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
683:  *
684:  * Returned Value:
685:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
686:  *
687:  ****************************************************************************/
688: 
689: static int gt9xx_close(FAR struct file *filep)
690: {
691:   FAR struct inode *inode;
692:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
693:   int use_count;
694:   int ret;
695: 
696:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
697: 
698:   iinfo("\n");
699:   inode = filep->f_inode;
700:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
701:   priv = inode->i_private;
702: 
703:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
704: 
705:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
706:   if (ret < 0)
707:     {
708:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
709:       return ret;
710:     }
711: 
712:   /* Decrement the Reference Count */
713: 
714:   use_count = priv->cref - 1;
715:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count >= 0);
716:   if (use_count == 0)
717:     {
718:       /* If final user, disable Touch Panel Interrupts */
719: 
720:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board && priv->board->irq_enable);
721:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, false);
722: 
723:       /* Power off the Touch Panel */
724: 
725:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power);
726:       priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
727:     }
728: 
729:   /* Set the Reference Count */
730: 
731:   priv->cref = use_count;
732: 
733:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
734: 
735:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
736:   return OK;
737: }

739: /****************************************************************************
740:  * Name: gt9xx_poll
741:  *
742:  * Description:
743:  *   Setup or teardown a poll for the Touch Panel Device.
744:  *
745:  * Input Parameters:
746:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
747:  *   fds   - The structure describing the events to be monitored, OR NULL if
748:  *           this is a request to stop monitoring events.
749:  *   setup - true: Setup the poll; false: Teardown the poll
750:  *
751:  * Returned Value:
752:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
753:  *
754:  ****************************************************************************/
755: 
756: static int gt9xx_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
757:                       bool setup)
758: {
759:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
760:   FAR struct inode *inode;
761:   bool pending;
762:   int ret = 0;
763:   int i;
764: 
765:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
766: 
767:   iinfo("setup=%d\n", setup);
768:   DEBUGASSERT(fds);
769:   inode = filep->f_inode;
770:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
771:   priv = inode->i_private;
772: 
773:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Poll Waiters */
774: 
775:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
776:   if (ret < 0)
777:     {
778:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
779:       return ret;
780:     }
781: 
782:   if (setup)
783:     {
784:       /* If Poll Setup: Ignore waits that do not include POLLIN */
785: 
786:       if ((fds->events & POLLIN) == 0)
787:         {
788:           ret = -EDEADLK;
789:           goto out;
790:         }
791: 
792:       /* Find an available slot for the Poll Waiter */
793: 
794:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS; i++)
795:         {
796:           /* Found an available slot */
797: 
798:           if (!priv->fds[i])
799:             {
800:               /* Bind the poll structure and this slot */
801: 
802:               priv->fds[i] = fds;
803:               fds->priv = &priv->fds[i];
804:               break;
805:             }
806:         }
807: 
808:       if (i >= CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS)
809:         {
810:           /* No slots available */
811: 
812:           fds->priv = NULL;
813:           ret = -EBUSY;
814:         }
815:       else
816:         {
817:           /* If Interrupt Pending is set, notify the Poll Waiters */
818: 
819:           pending = priv->int_pending;
820:           if (pending)
821:             {
822:               poll_notify(&fds, 1, POLLIN);
823:             }
824:         }
825:     }
826:   else if (fds->priv)
827:     {
828:       /* If Poll Teardown: Remove the poll setup */
829: 
830:       FAR struct pollfd **slot = (FAR struct pollfd **)fds->priv;
831:       DEBUGASSERT(slot != NULL);
832: 
833:       *slot = NULL;
834:       fds->priv = NULL;
835:     }
836: 
837:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Poll Waiters */
838: 
839: out:
840:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
841:   return ret;
842: }

844: /****************************************************************************
845:  * Name: gt9xx_isr_handler
846:  *
847:  * Description:
848:  *   Interrupt Handler for Touch Panel.
849:  *
850:  * Input Parameters:
851:  *   irq     - IRQ Number
852:  *   context - IRQ Context
853:  *   arg     - Touch Panel Device
854:  *
855:  * Returned Value:
856:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
857:  *
858:  ****************************************************************************/
859: 
860: static int gt9xx_isr_handler(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
861: {
862:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *)arg;
863:   irqstate_t flags;
864: 
865:   DEBUGASSERT(priv);
866: 
867:   /* Begin Critical Section */
868: 
869:   flags = enter_critical_section();
870: 
871:   /* Set the Interrupt Pending Flag */
872: 
873:   priv->int_pending = true;
874: 
875:   /* End Critical Section */
876: 
877:   leave_critical_section(flags);
878: 
879:   /* Notify the Poll Waiters */
880: 
881:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
882:   return OK;
883: }

23: /* The TOUCHSCREEN driver exports a standard character driver interface. By
24:  * convention, the touchscreen driver is registers as an input device at
25:  * /dev/inputN where N uniquely identifies the driver instance.
26:  *
27:  * This header file documents the generic interface that all NuttX
28:  * touchscreen devices must conform.  It adds standards and conventions on
29:  * top of the standard character driver interface.
30:  */
31: 
32: #ifndef __INCLUDE_NUTTX_INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN_H
33: #define __INCLUDE_NUTTX_INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN_H
34: 
35: /****************************************************************************
36:  * Included Files
37:  ****************************************************************************/
38: 
39: #include <nuttx/config.h>
40: #include <nuttx/fs/ioctl.h>
41: #include <nuttx/circbuf.h>
42: #include <nuttx/semaphore_type.h>
43: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
44: #include <time.h>
45: #include <inttypes.h>
46: #include <fixedmath.h>
47: 
48: /****************************************************************************
49:  * Pre-processor Definitions
50:  ****************************************************************************/
51: 
52: /* IOCTL Commands ***********************************************************/
53: 
54: /* Common TSC IOCTL commands */
55: 
56: #define TSIOC_SETXRCAL       _TSIOC(0x0001) /* arg: Pointer to
57:                                              * int Xplate R calibration value
58:                                              */
59: #define TSIOC_GETXRCAL       _TSIOC(0x0002) /* arg: Pointer to
60:                                              * int Xplate R calibration value
61:                                              */
62: #define TSIOC_SETFREQUENCY   _TSIOC(0x0003) /* arg: Pointer to
63:                                              * uint32_t frequency value
64:                                              */
65: #define TSIOC_GETFREQUENCY   _TSIOC(0x0004) /* arg: Pointer to
66:                                              *  uint32_t frequency value
67:                                              */
68: #define TSIOC_GETFWVERSION   _TSIOC(0x0005) /* arg: Pointer to
69:                                              * uint32_t firmware version
70:                                              * value
71:                                              * */
72: #define TSIOC_ENABLEGESTURE  _TSIOC(0x0006) /* arg: Pointer to
73:                                              * int for enable gesture feature
74:                                              */
75: #define TSIOC_DOACALIB       _TSIOC(0x0007) /* arg: none.
76:                                              * Initiate TS auto calibration
77:                                              */
78: #define TSIOC_CALDATA        _TSIOC(0x0008) /* arg: Pointer to
79:                                              * struct g_tscaldata_s
80:                                              */
81: #define TSIOC_USESCALED      _TSIOC(0x0009) /* arg: bool, yes/no */
82: #define TSIOC_GETOFFSETX     _TSIOC(0x000a) /* arg: Pointer to
83:                                              * int X offset value
84:                                              */
85: #define TSIOC_GETOFFSETY     _TSIOC(0x000b) /* arg: Pointer to
86:                                              * int Y offset value
87:                                              */
88: #define TSIOC_GETTHRESHX     _TSIOC(0x000c) /* arg: Pointer to
89:                                              * int X threshold value
90:                                              */
91: #define TSIOC_GETTHRESHY     _TSIOC(0x000d) /* arg: Pointer to
92:                                              * int Y threshold value
93:                                              */
94: 
95: #define TSIOC_GRAB           _TSIOC(0x000e) /* arg: Pointer to
96:                                              * int for enable grab
97:                                              */
98: 
99: #define TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS   _TSIOC(0x000f) /* arg: Pointer to
100:                                              * uint8_t max touch point
101:                                              */
102: #define TSIOC_GETRESOLUTION  _TSIOC(0x0010) /* arg: Pointer to
103:                                              * struct touch_resolution_s
104:                                              */
105: 
106: #define TSC_FIRST            0x0001          /* First common command */
107: #define TSC_NCMDS            16              /* Fifteenth common commands */
108: 
109: /* Backward compatible IOCTL */
110: 
111: #define TSIOC_SETCALIB       TSIOC_SETXRCAL
112: #define TSIOC_GETCALIB       TSIOC_GETXRCAL
113: 
114: /* User defined ioctl commands are also supported.  However, the
115:  * TSC driver must reserve a block of commands as follows in order
116:  * prevent IOCTL command numbers from overlapping.
117:  *
118:  * This is generally done as follows.  The first reservation for
119:  * TSC driver A would look like:
120:  *
121:  *   TSC_A_FIRST         (TSC_FIRST + TSC_NCMDS)     <- First command
122:  *   TSC_A_NCMDS         42                          <- Number of commands
123:  *
124:  * IOCTL commands for TSC driver A would then be defined in a
125:  * TSC A header file like:
126:  *
127:  *   TSCIOC_A_CMD1       _TSIOC(TSC_A_FIRST + 0)
128:  *   TSCIOC_A_CMD2       _TSIOC(TSC_A_FIRST + 1)
129:  *   TSCIOC_A_CMD3       _TSIOC(TSC_A_FIRST + 2)
130:  *   ...
131:  *   TSCIOC_A_CMD42      _TSIOC(TSC_A_FIRST + 41)
132:  *
133:  * The next reservation would look like:
134:  *
135:  *   TSC_B_FIRST         (TSC_A_FIRST + TSC_A_NCMDS) <- Next command
136:  *   TSC_B_NCMDS         77                          <- Number of commands
137:  */
138: 
139: /* These definitions provide the meaning of all of the bits that may be
140:  * reported in the struct touch_point_s flags.
141:  */
142: 
143: #define TOUCH_DOWN           (1 << 0) /* A new touch contact is established */
144: #define TOUCH_MOVE           (1 << 1) /* Movement occurred with previously reported contact */
145: #define TOUCH_UP             (1 << 2) /* The touch contact was lost */
146: #define TOUCH_ID_VALID       (1 << 3) /* Touch ID is certain */
147: #define TOUCH_POS_VALID      (1 << 4) /* Hardware provided a valid X/Y position */
148: #define TOUCH_PRESSURE_VALID (1 << 5) /* Hardware provided a valid pressure */
149: #define TOUCH_SIZE_VALID     (1 << 6) /* Hardware provided a valid H/W contact size */
150: #define TOUCH_GESTURE_VALID  (1 << 7) /* Hardware provided a valid gesture */
151: 
152: /* These are definitions for touch gesture */
153: 
154: #define TOUCH_SINGLE_CLICK   (0x00)
155: #define TOUCH_DOUBLE_CLICK   (0x01)
156: #define TOUCH_SLIDE_UP       (0x02)
157: #define TOUCH_SLIDE_DOWN     (0x03)
158: #define TOUCH_SLIDE_LEFT     (0x04)
159: #define TOUCH_SLIDE_RIGHT    (0x05)
160: #define TOUCH_PALM           (0x06)
161: 
162: /* Help function */
163: 
164: #define SCALE_TS(x, o, s)     (b16toi(b16divb16(((x) - (o)), (s))))
165: 
166: /****************************************************************************
167:  * Public Types
168:  ****************************************************************************/
169: 
170: /* This struct is used to store touchscreen calibration data for use by
171:  * low level touichscreen drivers.
172:  *
173:  * It is used as follows:
174:  *
175:  *   scaledX = (raw_x - offset_x) / slope_x
176:  *   scaledY = (raw_y - offset_y) / slope_y
177:  *
178:  * The calibration values would typically be derived by taking top left and
179:  * bottom right measurements on the actual LCD/touchscreen used:
180:  *
181:  * xSlope  = (ActualRightX -  ActualLeftX) / (WantedRightX - WantedLeftX)
182:  * xOffset =  ActualLeftX  - (WantedLeftX * xSlope)
183:  *
184:  * And similarly for the Y values.
185:  *
186:  * ySlope  = (ActualBottomY -  ActualTopY) / (WantedBottomY - WantedTopY)
187:  * yOffset =  ActualTopY    - (WantedTopY * ySlope)
188:  *
189:  */
190: 
191:   struct g_tscaldata_s
192:   {
193:     b16_t slope_x;
194:     b16_t offset_x;
195:     b16_t slope_y;
196:     b16_t offset_y;
197:   };
198: 
199: /* This struct is used to get touchscreen resolution data for use by
200:  * application.
201:  */
202: 
203: begin_packed_struct struct touch_resolution_s
204: {
205:   uint16_t res_x;
206:   uint16_t res_y;
207: } end_packed_struct;
208: 
209: /* This structure contains information about a single touch point.
210:  * Positional units are device specific.
211:  */
212: 
213: begin_packed_struct struct touch_point_s
214: {
215:   uint8_t  id;        /* Unique identifies contact; Same in all reports for the contact */
216:   uint8_t  flags;     /* See TOUCH_* definitions above */
217:   int16_t  x;         /* X coordinate of the touch point (uncalibrated) */
218:   int16_t  y;         /* Y coordinate of the touch point (uncalibrated) */
219:   int16_t  h;         /* Height of touch point (uncalibrated) */
220:   int16_t  w;         /* Width of touch point (uncalibrated) */
221:   uint16_t gesture;   /* Gesture of touchscreen contact */
222:   uint16_t pressure;  /* Touch pressure */
223:   uint16_t dummy;     /* Padded with 2 bytes here */
224:   uint64_t timestamp; /* Touch event time stamp, in microseconds */
225: } end_packed_struct;
226: 
227: /* The typical touchscreen driver is a read-only, input character device
228:  * driver.the driver write() method is not supported and any attempt to
229:  * open the driver in any mode other than read-only will fail.
230:  *
231:  * Data read from the touchscreen device consists only of touch events and
232:  * touch sample data.  This is reflected by struct touch_sample_s.  This
233:  * structure is returned by either the driver read method.
234:  *
235:  * On some devices, multiple touchpoints may be supported. So this top level
236:  * data structure is a struct touch_sample_s that "contains" a set of touch
237:  * points.  Each touch point is managed individually using an ID that
238:  * identifies a touch from first contact until the end of the contact.
239:  */
240: 
241: begin_packed_struct struct touch_sample_s
242: {
243:   int32_t npoints;               /* The number of touch points in point[] */
244:   int32_t dummy;                 /* Padded with 4 bytes here */
245:   struct touch_point_s point[1]; /* Actual dimension is npoints */
246: } end_packed_struct;
247: 
248: #define SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(n) \
249:   (sizeof(struct touch_sample_s) + ((n) - 1) * sizeof(struct touch_point_s))
250: 
251: #ifdef CONFIG_INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN
252: 
253: /* This structure is for touchscreen lower half driver */
254: 
255: struct touch_lowerhalf_s
256: {
257:   uint8_t       maxpoint;       /* Maximal point supported by the touchscreen */
258:   FAR void      *priv;          /* Save the upper half pointer */
259: 
260:   /**************************************************************************
261:    * Name: control
262:    *
263:    * Description:
264:    *   Users can use this interface to implement custom IOCTL.
265:    *
266:    * Arguments:
267:    *   lower   - The instance of lower half of touchscreen device.
268:    *   cmd     - User defined specific command.
269:    *   arg     - Argument of the specific command.
270:    *
271:    * Return Value:
272:    *   Zero(OK) on success; a negated errno value on failure.
273:    *   -ENOTTY - The command is not supported.
274:    **************************************************************************/
275: 
276:   CODE int (*control)(FAR struct touch_lowerhalf_s *lower,
277:                       int cmd, unsigned long arg);
278: 
279:   /**************************************************************************
280:    * Name: write
281:    *
282:    * Description:
283:    *   Users can use this interface to implement custom write.
284:    *
285:    * Arguments:
286:    *   lower   - The instance of lower half of touchscreen device.
287:    *   buffer  - User defined specific buffer.
288:    *   buflen  - User defined specific buffer size.
289:    *
290:    * Return Value:
291:    *   Number of bytes written；a negated errno value on failure.
292:    *
293:    **************************************************************************/
294: 
295:   CODE ssize_t (*write)(FAR struct touch_lowerhalf_s *lower,
296:                         FAR const char *buffer, size_t buflen);
297: };
298: 
299: /****************************************************************************
300:  * Inline Functions
301:  ****************************************************************************/
302: 
303: static inline uint64_t touch_get_time(void)
304: {
305:   struct timespec ts;
306: 
307:   clock_systime_timespec(&ts);
308:   return 1000000ull * ts.tv_sec + ts.tv_nsec / 1000;
309: }
310:

312:  * Public Function Prototypes

314: 
315: /****************************************************************************

318:  * Description:

322:  * Arguments:

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * arch/arm64/src/s6/s6_gpio.c
3:  *
4:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5:  *
6:  ****************************************************************************/
7: 
8: /* Minimal GPIO support for the Amlogic S6 periphs GPIOA bank and the GPIO
9:  * interrupt controller (SC2-style).  Register layout follows the vendor
10:  * pinctrl / gpio-intc drivers.
11:  */
12: 
13: /****************************************************************************
14:  * Included Files
15:  ****************************************************************************/
16: 
17: #include <nuttx/config.h>
18: 
19: #include <errno.h>
20: 
21: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
22: 
23: #include "arm64_internal.h"
24: #include "s6_gpio.h"
25: #include "hardware/s6_gpio.h"
26: 
27: #ifdef CONFIG_S6_GPIO
28: 
29: /****************************************************************************
30:  * Public Functions
31:  ****************************************************************************/
32: 
33: /****************************************************************************
34:  * Name: s6_gpioa_set_mux
35:  *
36:  * Description:
37:  *   Select the peripheral function of a GPIOA pin (0-15); function 0 is
38:  *   the plain GPIO function.
39:  *
40:  ****************************************************************************/
41: 
42: int s6_gpioa_set_mux(uint8_t pin, uint8_t func)
43: {
44:   if (pin >= S6_GPIOA_NPINS)
45:     {
46:       return -EINVAL;
47:     }
48: 
49:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_MUX_BASE + S6_GPIOA_MUX_OFFSET(pin),
50:               0xfu << S6_GPIOA_MUX_SHIFT(pin),
51:               (func & 0xfu) << S6_GPIOA_MUX_SHIFT(pin));
52:   return OK;
53: }
54: 
55: /****************************************************************************
56:  * Name: s6_gpioa_write
57:  *
58:  * Description:
59:  *   Set the output level of a GPIOA pin (0-15).
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: void s6_gpioa_write(uint8_t pin, bool value)
64: {
65:   DEBUGASSERT(pin < S6_GPIOA_NPINS);
66: 
67:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_GPIO_BASE + S6_GPIOA_OUT_OFFSET,
68:               1u << pin, value ? (1u << pin) : 0);
69: }
70: 
71: /****************************************************************************
72:  * Name: s6_gpioa_config_input
73:  *
74:  * Description:
75:  *   Configure a GPIOA pin (0-15) as a plain GPIO input.
76:  *
77:  ****************************************************************************/
78: 
79: int s6_gpioa_config_input(uint8_t pin)
80: {
81:   int ret;
82: 
83:   ret = s6_gpioa_set_mux(pin, 0);
84:   if (ret < 0)
85:     {
86:       return ret;
87:     }
88: 
89:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_GPIO_BASE + S6_GPIOA_DIR_OFFSET,
90:               1u << pin, 1u << pin);
91:   return OK;
92: }
93: 
94: /****************************************************************************
95:  * Name: s6_gpioa_config_output
96:  *
97:  * Description:
98:  *   Configure a GPIOA pin (0-15) as a plain GPIO output with an initial
99:  *   level.
100:  *
101:  ****************************************************************************/
102: 
103: int s6_gpioa_config_output(uint8_t pin, bool value)
104: {
105:   int ret;
106: 
107:   ret = s6_gpioa_set_mux(pin, 0);
108:   if (ret < 0)
109:     {
110:       return ret;
111:     }
112: 
113:   s6_gpioa_write(pin, value);
114:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_GPIO_BASE + S6_GPIOA_DIR_OFFSET, 1u << pin, 0);
115:   return OK;
116: }
117: 
118: /****************************************************************************
119:  * Name: s6_gpioint_config
120:  *
121:  * Description:
122:  *   Route a GPIO (global number, e.g. S6_GPIOA(10)) to a GPIO interrupt
123:  *   controller channel (0-11) and program its trigger type.  The interrupt
124:  *   then arrives on GIC INTID 42 + channel; masking happens at the GIC.
125:  *
126:  * Input Parameters:
127:  *   channel - GPIO interrupt controller channel (0-11)
128:  *   gpio    - Global GPIO number
129:  *   trigger - One of the IRQ_* trigger modes from nuttx/arch.h
130:  *
131:  ****************************************************************************/
132: 
133: int s6_gpioint_config(uint8_t channel, uint8_t gpio, int trigger)
134: {
135:   uint32_t reg;
136:   uint32_t val = 0;
137: 
138:   if (channel >= S6_GPIOINT_NCHANNELS)
139:     {
140:       return -EINVAL;
141:     }
142: 
143:   /* Global interrupt switch (harmless to re-set) */
144: 
145:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_INTC_BASE + S6_GPIOINT_EDGE_POL_OFFSET,
146:               0, S6_GPIOINT_GLOBAL_EN);
147: 
148:   /* Bind the GPIO number to the channel */
149: 
150:   reg = S6_GPIO_INTC_BASE + S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_OFFSET(channel);
151:   modifyreg32(reg, S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_MASK(channel),
152:               (gpio << S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_SHIFT(channel)) &
153:               S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_MASK(channel));
154: 
155:   /* Configure the trigger type. */
156: 
157:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_INTC_BASE + S6_GPIOINT_EDGE_POL_EXTR_OFFSET,
158:               S6_GPIOINT_BOTH(channel),
159:               trigger == IRQ_BOTH_EDGE ? S6_GPIOINT_BOTH(channel) : 0);
160: 
161:   if (trigger == IRQ_FALLING_EDGE || trigger == IRQ_LOW_LEVEL)
162:     {
163:       val |= S6_GPIOINT_POL_LOW(channel);
164:     }
165: 
166:   if (trigger == IRQ_RISING_EDGE || trigger == IRQ_FALLING_EDGE)
167:     {
168:       val |= S6_GPIOINT_EDGE(channel);
169:     }
170: 
171:   modifyreg32(S6_GPIO_INTC_BASE + S6_GPIOINT_EDGE_POL_OFFSET,
172:               S6_GPIOINT_POL_LOW(channel) | S6_GPIOINT_EDGE(channel), val);
173:   return OK;
174: }
175: 
176: #endif /* CONFIG_S6_GPIO */
