1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * arch/arm64/src/s6/s6_i2c.c
3:  *
4:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5:  *
6:  ****************************************************************************/
7: 
8: /****************************************************************************
9:  * Included Files
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/config.h>
13: 
14: #include <stdbool.h>
15: #include <stdint.h>
16: #include <errno.h>
17: 
18: #include <arch/chip/chip.h>
19: #include <debug.h>
20: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
21: #include <nuttx/mutex.h>
22: 
23: #include "arm64_internal.h"
24: #include "s6_i2c.h"
25: #include "hardware/s6_i2c.h"
26: 
27: #ifdef CONFIG_S6_I2C
28: 
29: /****************************************************************************
30:  * Pre-processor Definitions
31:  ****************************************************************************/
32: 
33: /* Timeout for a single token chunk */
34: 
35: #define S6_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS         500
36: #define S6_I2C_POLL_DELAY_US      50
37: #define S6_I2C_POLL_COUNT \
38:   (S6_I2C_TIMEOUT_MS * 1000 / S6_I2C_POLL_DELAY_US)
39: 
40: /* Data bytes per token chunk (RDATA/WDATA registers hold 8 bytes) */
41: 
42: #define S6_I2C_CHUNK_SIZE         8
43: 
44: #define DIV_ROUND_UP(n, d)        (((n) + (d) - 1) / (d))
45: 
46: /****************************************************************************
47:  * Private Types
48:  ****************************************************************************/
49: 
50: /* I2C device private data */
51: 
52: struct s6_i2c_dev_s
53: {
54:   struct i2c_master_s dev;    /* I2C master device (must be first) */
55:   uintptr_t base;             /* Controller base address */
56:   uint32_t frequency;         /* Configured bus frequency */
57:   mutex_t  lock;              /* Serialize transfers on the bus */
58: };
59: 
60: /****************************************************************************
61:  * Private Function Prototypes
62:  ****************************************************************************/
63: 
64: static int s6_i2c_transfer(struct i2c_master_s *dev,
65:                            struct i2c_msg_s *msgs, int count);
66: 
67: /****************************************************************************
68:  * Private Data
69:  ****************************************************************************/
70: 
71: static const struct i2c_ops_s g_s6_i2c_ops =
72: {
73:   .transfer = s6_i2c_transfer
74: };
75: 
76: static struct s6_i2c_dev_s g_s6_i2c0 =
77: {
78:   .dev       =
79:     {
80:       .ops = &g_s6_i2c_ops
81:     },
82:   .base      = CONFIG_S6_I2C0_BASE,
83:   .frequency = 0,
84:   .lock      = NXMUTEX_INITIALIZER
85: };
86: 
87: /****************************************************************************
88:  * Private Functions
89:  ****************************************************************************/
90: 
91: /****************************************************************************
92:  * Name: s6_i2c_set_clk_div
93:  *
94:  * Description:
95:  *   Install the SCL high/low dividers for the requested bus frequency,
96:  *   following the vendor (AMLOGIC_MODIFY) divider algorithm.
97:  *
98:  ****************************************************************************/
99: 
100: static void s6_i2c_set_clk_div(FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv,
101:                                uint32_t frequency)
102: {
103:   uint32_t div_temp;
104:   uint32_t div_h;
105:   uint32_t div_l;
106: 
107:   if (frequency >= 400000)
108:     {
109:       /* Fast mode: H/L duty 2/3 */
110: 
111:       div_temp = DIV_ROUND_UP(CONFIG_S6_I2C_CLK_HZ * 2, frequency * 5);
112:       div_h    = div_temp - 15;
113:       div_l    = DIV_ROUND_UP(CONFIG_S6_I2C_CLK_HZ * 3, frequency * 10);
114:     }
115:   else
116:     {
117:       /* Standard mode: 50% duty */
118: 
119:       div_temp = DIV_ROUND_UP(CONFIG_S6_I2C_CLK_HZ, frequency);
120:       div_h    = DIV_ROUND_UP(div_temp, 2) - 15;
121:       div_l    = DIV_ROUND_UP(div_temp, 4);
122:     }
123: 
124:   /* The divider fields are 12 bits wide */
125: 
126:   if (div_h >= (1 << 12))
127:     {
128:       div_h = (1 << 12) - 1;
129:     }
130: 
131:   if (div_l >= (1 << 12))
132:     {
133:       div_l = (1 << 12) - 1;
134:     }
135: 
136:   iinfo("freq %u, div_h %u, div_l %u\n", frequency, div_h, div_l);
137: 
138:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET,
139:               S6_I2C_CTRL_CLKDIV_MASK,
140:               (div_h & 0x3ff) << S6_I2C_CTRL_CLKDIV_SHIFT);
141:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET,
142:               S6_I2C_CTRL_CLKDIVEXT_MASK,
143:               (div_h >> 10) << S6_I2C_CTRL_CLKDIVEXT_SHIFT);
144:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_SLAVE_ADDR_OFFSET,
145:               S6_I2C_SLV_DIVL_MASK,
146:               (div_l << S6_I2C_SLV_DIVL_SHIFT) & S6_I2C_SLV_DIVL_MASK);
147:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_SLAVE_ADDR_OFFSET,
148:               S6_I2C_SLV_DIVL_EN, S6_I2C_SLV_DIVL_EN);
149: }
150: 
151: /****************************************************************************
152:  * Name: s6_i2c_add_token
153:  *
154:  * Description:
155:  *   Append a token command to the packed token list (up to 8 per register).
156:  *
157:  ****************************************************************************/
158: 
159: static void s6_i2c_add_token(FAR uint64_t *tokens, FAR int *ntok, int token)
160: {
161:   *tokens |= (uint64_t)token << (*ntok * 4);
162:   (*ntok)++;
163: }
164: 
165: /****************************************************************************
166:  * Name: s6_i2c_put_data
167:  *
168:  * Description:
169:  *   Pack up to eight bytes into the controller's write data registers.
170:  *
171:  ****************************************************************************/
172: 
173: static void s6_i2c_put_data(FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv,
174:                             FAR const uint8_t *buffer, int length)
175: {
176:   uint32_t data[2] =
177:   {
178:     0, 0
179:   };
180: 
181:   int i;
182: 
183:   for (i = 0; i < length; i++)
184:     {
185:       data[i >> 2] |= (uint32_t)buffer[i] << ((i & 3) * 8);
186:     }
187: 
188:   putreg32(data[0], priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_WDATA0_OFFSET);
189:   putreg32(data[1], priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_WDATA1_OFFSET);
190: }
191: 
192: /****************************************************************************
193:  * Name: s6_i2c_get_data
194:  *
195:  * Description:
196:  *   Unpack up to eight bytes from the controller's read data registers.
197:  *
198:  ****************************************************************************/
199: 
200: static void s6_i2c_get_data(FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv,
201:                             FAR uint8_t *buffer, int length)
202: {
203:   uint32_t data[2];
204:   int i;
205: 
206:   data[0] = getreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_RDATA0_OFFSET);
207:   data[1] = getreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_RDATA1_OFFSET);
208: 
209:   for (i = 0; i < length; i++)
210:     {
211:       buffer[i] = (data[i >> 2] >> ((i & 3) * 8)) & 0xff;
212:     }
213: }
214: 
215: /****************************************************************************
216:  * Name: s6_i2c_run_tokens
217:  *
218:  * Description:
219:  *   Write the token list, run it on the 0 -> 1 edge of START and poll until
220:  *   the controller finishes.  Returns -ENXIO on a NAK and -ETIMEDOUT when a
221:  *   chunk does not complete in time (aborting the controller).
222:  *
223:  ****************************************************************************/
224: 
225: static int s6_i2c_run_tokens(FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv, uint64_t tokens)
226: {
227:   uint32_t timeout = S6_I2C_POLL_COUNT;
228:   uint32_t ctrl;
229: 
230:   putreg32((uint32_t)tokens, priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_LIST0_OFFSET);
231:   putreg32((uint32_t)(tokens >> 32), priv->base + S6_I2C_TOK_LIST1_OFFSET);
232: 
233:   /* A chunk runs on every 0 -> 1 transition of START */
234: 
235:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET, S6_I2C_CTRL_START, 0);
236:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET,
237:               S6_I2C_CTRL_START, S6_I2C_CTRL_START);
238: 
239:   for (;;)
240:     {
241:       ctrl = getreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET);
242:       if ((ctrl & S6_I2C_CTRL_STATUS) == 0)
243:         {
244:           /* The controller is idle; the same read tells a NAK from a
245:            * clean completion.
246:            */
247: 
248:           if ((ctrl & S6_I2C_CTRL_ERROR) != 0)
249:             {
250:               ierr("NAK\n");
251:               return -ENXIO;
252:             }
253: 
254:           return OK;
255:         }
256: 
257:       if (--timeout == 0)
258:         {
259:           /* Abort anything left running */
260: 
261:           modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET,
262:                       S6_I2C_CTRL_START, 0);
263:           ierr("transfer timeout\n");
264:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
265:         }
266: 
267:       up_udelay(S6_I2C_POLL_DELAY_US);
268:     }
269: }
270: 
271: /****************************************************************************
272:  * Name: s6_i2c_xfer_msg
273:  *
274:  * Description:
275:  *   Transfer one message in token chunks of at most 8 data bytes.  When
276:  *   'cont' is set the transfer continues in a NOSTART follow-up message,
277:  *   so no STOP is issued and a read is not NAKed yet.
278:  *
279:  ****************************************************************************/
280: 
281: static int s6_i2c_xfer_msg(FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv,
282:                            FAR struct i2c_msg_s *msg, bool cont)
283: {
284:   bool write = (msg->flags & I2C_M_READ) == 0;
285:   bool stop = !cont && (msg->flags & I2C_M_NOSTOP) == 0;
286:   int len = msg->length;
287:   int pos = 0;
288: 
289:   iinfo("addr %02x len %d flags %04x\n", msg->addr, len, msg->flags);
290: 
291:   /* START and the slave address only appear in the first chunk */
292: 
293:   if ((msg->flags & I2C_M_NOSTART) == 0)
294:     {
295:       modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_SLAVE_ADDR_OFFSET,
296:                   S6_I2C_SLV_ADDR_MASK,
297:                   (msg->addr << 1) & S6_I2C_SLV_ADDR_MASK);
298:     }
299: 
300:   /* Reconfigure the dividers only when the frequency changes */
301: 
302:   if (msg->frequency != 0 && msg->frequency != priv->frequency)
303:     {
304:       s6_i2c_set_clk_div(priv, msg->frequency);
305:       priv->frequency = msg->frequency;
306:     }
307: 
308:   do
309:     {
310:       uint64_t tokens = 0;
311:       int ntok = 0;
312:       int count = len - pos;
313:       int i;
314:       int ret;
315: 
316:       if (count > S6_I2C_CHUNK_SIZE)
317:         {
318:           count = S6_I2C_CHUNK_SIZE;
319:         }
320: 
321:       if (pos == 0 && (msg->flags & I2C_M_NOSTART) == 0)
322:         {
323:           s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, S6_I2C_TOKEN_START);
324:           s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, write ?
325:                            S6_I2C_TOKEN_SLAVE_ADDR_WRITE :
326:                            S6_I2C_TOKEN_SLAVE_ADDR_READ);
327:         }
328: 
329:       for (i = 0; i < count - 1; i++)
330:         {
331:           s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, S6_I2C_TOKEN_DATA);
332:         }
333: 
334:       if (count > 0)
335:         {
336:           /* The final byte of a read message must be NAKed, unless more
337:            * data follows in this message or a NOSTART follow-up message.
338:            */
339: 
340:           if (write || pos + count < len || cont)
341:             {
342:               s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, S6_I2C_TOKEN_DATA);
343:             }
344:           else
345:             {
346:               s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, S6_I2C_TOKEN_DATA_LAST);
347:             }
348:         }
349: 
350:       if (stop && pos + count >= len)
351:         {
352:           s6_i2c_add_token(&tokens, &ntok, S6_I2C_TOKEN_STOP);
353:         }
354: 
355:       if (write && count > 0)
356:         {
357:           s6_i2c_put_data(priv, &msg->buffer[pos], count);
358:         }
359: 
360:       ret = s6_i2c_run_tokens(priv, tokens);
361:       if (ret < 0)
362:         {
363:           return ret;
364:         }
365: 
366:       if (!write)
367:         {
368:           s6_i2c_get_data(priv, &msg->buffer[pos], count);
369:         }
370: 
371:       pos += count;
372:     }
373:   while (pos < len);
374: 
375:   return OK;
376: }
377: 
378: /****************************************************************************
379:  * Name: s6_i2c_transfer
380:  *
381:  * Description:
382:  *   Validate and perform a sequence of I2C messages on the bus.
383:  *
384:  ****************************************************************************/
385: 
386: static int s6_i2c_transfer(struct i2c_master_s *dev,
387:                            FAR struct i2c_msg_s *msgs, int count)
388: {
389:   FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *)dev;
390:   uint32_t ctrl;
391:   int ret = OK;
392:   int i;
393: 
394:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && msgs != NULL && count > 0);
395: 
396:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
397:   if (ret < 0)
398:     {
399:       return ret;
400:     }
401: 
402:   /* Both lines held low means the bus is not usable (no pull-ups) */
403: 
404:   ctrl = getreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET);
405:   if ((ctrl & (S6_I2C_CTRL_SCL_LEVEL | S6_I2C_CTRL_SDA_LEVEL)) == 0)
406:     {
407:       ierr("SCL and SDA are low, no pull-up?\n");
408:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
409:       return -ENXIO;
410:     }
411: 
412:   for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
413:     {
414:       /* A NOSTART message continues the previous one, so it must follow a
415:        * message to the same slave in the same direction.
416:        */
417: 
418:       if ((msgs[i].flags & I2C_M_NOSTART) != 0 &&
419:           (i == 0 || msgs[i].addr != msgs[i - 1].addr ||
420:            ((msgs[i].flags ^ msgs[i - 1].flags) & I2C_M_READ) != 0))
421:         {
422:           ret = -EINVAL;
423:           break;
424:         }
425: 
426:       if ((msgs[i].flags & I2C_M_TEN) != 0)
427:         {
428:           ret = -ENOTSUP;
429:           break;
430:         }
431: 
432:       if (msgs[i].addr > 0x7f || msgs[i].length < 0 ||
433:           (msgs[i].length > 0 && msgs[i].buffer == NULL) ||
434:           msgs[i].frequency > I2C_SPEED_HIGH)
435:         {
436:           ret = -EINVAL;
437:           break;
438:         }
439: 
440:       /* Suppress the STOP when the next message continues this one */
441: 
442:       ret = s6_i2c_xfer_msg(priv, &msgs[i],
443:                             i + 1 < count &&
444:                             (msgs[i + 1].flags & I2C_M_NOSTART) != 0);
445:       if (ret < 0)
446:         {
447:           break;
448:         }
449:     }
450: 
451:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
452:   return (ret < 0) ? ret : count;
453: }
454: 
455: /****************************************************************************
456:  * Public Functions
457:  ****************************************************************************/
458: 
459: /****************************************************************************
460:  * Name: s6_i2cbus_initialize
461:  *
462:  * Description:
463:  *   Initialize the S6 I2C master (i2c0) and return its bus interface.
464:  *   The transfer engine is polled; no controller interrupt is used.
465:  *
466:  * Returned Value:
467:  *   The I2C0 master instance.
468:  *
469:  ****************************************************************************/
470: 
471: FAR struct i2c_master_s *s6_i2cbus_initialize(void)
472: {
473:   FAR struct s6_i2c_dev_s *priv = &g_s6_i2c0;
474: 
475:   /* Turn on the clock gate; a transfer triggers on the 0 -> 1 edge of
476:    * START, so leave it cleared with a known ACK/ERROR state.
477:    */
478: 
479:   modifyreg32(S6_CLK_SYS_CLK_EN0_REG1, 0, S6_I2C_GATE);
480:   modifyreg32(priv->base + S6_I2C_CTRL_OFFSET,
481:               S6_I2C_CTRL_START | S6_I2C_CTRL_ERROR |
482:               S6_I2C_CTRL_ACK_IGNORE, 0);
483: 
484:   s6_i2c_set_clk_div(priv, I2C_SPEED_STANDARD);
485:   priv->frequency = I2C_SPEED_STANDARD;
486: 
487:   iinfo("base %08lx\n", (unsigned long)priv->base);
488:   return &priv->dev;
489: }
490: 
491: #endif /* CONFIG_S6_I2C */

8: #ifndef __ARCH_ARM64_SRC_S6_HARDWARE_S6_GPIO_H

10: 
11: /****************************************************************************
12:  * Included Files

14: 
15: #include <nuttx/config.h>
16: #include <arch/chip/chip.h>
17: 
18: /****************************************************************************
19:  * Pre-processor Definitions
20:  ****************************************************************************/
21: 
22: /* Periphs pinctrl / GPIO interrupt controller base addresses */
23: 
24: #define S6_GPIO_MUX_BASE          (CONFIG_DEVICEIO_BASEADDR + 0x4000)
25: #define S6_GPIO_INTC_BASE         (CONFIG_DEVICEIO_BASEADDR + 0x4080)
26: #define S6_GPIO_GPIO_BASE         (CONFIG_DEVICEIO_BASEADDR + 0x40c0)
27: 
28: /* GPIOA bank registers.  The pinctrl driver stores register indices that
29:  * are word-scaled on access ((index + bit / 32) * 4), so the offsets below
30:  * are the resulting physical offsets from S6_GPIO_GPIO_BASE:
31:  *   OUT = 0x071 * 4 = 0x1c4
32:  *   DIR = 0x072 * 4 = 0x1c8 (EN_N semantics: bit set is input)
33:  */
34: 
35: #define S6_GPIOA_OUT_OFFSET       0x1c4
36: #define S6_GPIOA_DIR_OFFSET       0x1c8
37: 
38: /* GPIOA pin mux: bank index 0x010, word-scaled on access (x4), four bits
39:  * per pin (16 pins span two words, 8 pins each).
40:  */
41: 
42: #define S6_GPIOA_MUX_OFFSET(pin)  (0x040 + ((pin) >> 3) * 4)
43: #define S6_GPIOA_MUX_SHIFT(pin)   (((pin) & 7) * 4)
44: 
45: /* GPIO interrupt controller (12 channels mapped to GIC SPI 10..21, i.e.
46:  * GIC INTIDs 42..53).  Channel selection register layout:
47:  *   PIN_SEL(channel)   select register for the GPIO number
48:  *   EDGE_POL           bit(0+n): polarity low, bit(12+n): edge,
49:  *                      bit31: global enable switch
50:  *   EDGE_POL_EXTR      bit(n): both-edges mode
51:  */
52: 
53: #define S6_GPIOINT_EDGE_POL_OFFSET      0x00
54: #define S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_OFFSET(ch)   (0x04 + ((ch) >> 1) * 4)
55: #define S6_GPIOINT_EDGE_POL_EXTR_OFFSET 0x1c
56: 
57: #define S6_GPIOINT_GLOBAL_EN      (1u << 31)
58: #define S6_GPIOINT_POL_LOW(ch)    (1u << (ch))
59: #define S6_GPIOINT_EDGE(ch)       (1u << (12 + (ch)))
60: #define S6_GPIOINT_BOTH(ch)       (1u << (ch))
61: 
62: #define S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_SHIFT(ch)  (((ch) & 1) * 16)
63: #define S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_MASK(ch)   (0xffu << S6_GPIOINT_PIN_SEL_SHIFT(ch))
64: 
65: #endif /* __ARCH_ARM64_SRC_S6_HARDWARE_S6_GPIO_H */

1: /**
2:  * @file lv_nuttx_mouse.c
3:  *
4:  */
5: 
6: /*********************
7:  *      INCLUDES
8:  *********************/
9: 
10: #include "lv_nuttx_mouse.h"
11: 
12: #if LV_USE_NUTTX_MOUSE
13: 
14: #include <sys/types.h>
15: #include <stdio.h>
16: #include <stdlib.h>
17: #include <unistd.h>
18: #include <debug.h>
19: #include <errno.h>
20: #include <fcntl.h>
21: #include <nuttx/input/mouse.h>
22: #include "../../lvgl_private.h"
23: 
24: /*********************
25:  *      DEFINES
26:  *********************/
27: 
28: /**********************
29:  *      TYPEDEFS
30:  **********************/
31: 
32: typedef struct {
33:     int fd;
34:     lv_indev_state_t last_state;
35:     struct mouse_report_s last_sample;
36:     bool has_last_sample;
37: } lv_nuttx_mouse_t;
38: 
39: /**********************
40:  *  STATIC PROTOTYPES
41:  **********************/
42: static void mouse_set_cursor(lv_indev_t * indev, int32_t size);
43: static void mouse_read(lv_indev_t * drv, lv_indev_data_t * data);
44: static void mouse_delete_cb(lv_event_t * e);
45: static lv_indev_t * mouse_init(int fd);
46: 
47: /**********************
48:  *  STATIC VARIABLES
49:  **********************/
50: 
51: /**********************
52:  *      MACROS
53:  **********************/
54: 
55: /**********************
56:  *   GLOBAL FUNCTIONS
57:  **********************/
58: 
59: lv_indev_t * lv_nuttx_mouse_create(const char * dev_path)
60: {
61:     lv_indev_t * indev;
62:     int fd;
63: 
64:     LV_ASSERT_NULL(dev_path);
65:     LV_LOG_USER("mouse %s opening", dev_path);
66:     fd = open(dev_path, O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC);
67:     if(fd < 0) {
68:         LV_LOG_ERROR("Error: cannot open mouse device");
69:         return NULL;
70:     }
71: 
72:     LV_LOG_USER("mouse %s open success", dev_path);
73: 
74:     indev = mouse_init(fd);
75: 
76:     if(indev == NULL) {
77:         close(fd);
78:     }
79: 
80:     return indev;
81: }
82: 
83: /**********************
84:  *   STATIC FUNCTIONS
85:  **********************/
86: 
87: static bool mouse_read_sample(int fd, struct mouse_report_s * sample)
88: {
89:     int nbytes = read(fd, sample, sizeof(struct mouse_report_s));
90:     if(nbytes == sizeof(struct mouse_report_s)) {
91:         return true;
92:     }
93:     else {
94:         if(nbytes == -1) {
95:             if(errno != EAGAIN) {
96:                 LV_LOG_WARN("Read error: %s", strerror(errno));
97:             }
98:         }
99:         else if(nbytes != 0) {
100:             LV_LOG_WARN("Unexpected read size: %d", nbytes);
101:         }
102:         return false;
103:     }
104: }
105: 
106: static void conv_mouse_sample(lv_indev_t * drv,
107:                               lv_indev_data_t * data,
108:                               struct mouse_report_s * sample)
109: {
110:     lv_nuttx_mouse_t * mouse = drv->driver_data;
111:     uint8_t mouse_buttons = sample->buttons;
112: 
113:     lv_display_t * disp = lv_indev_get_display(drv);
114:     int32_t hor_max = lv_display_get_horizontal_resolution(disp) - 1;
115:     int32_t ver_max = lv_display_get_vertical_resolution(disp) - 1;
116: 
117:     data->point.x =
118:         LV_CLAMP(0,
119:                  data->point.x + (sample->x * CONFIG_LV_MOUSE_RATE),
120:                  hor_max);
121:     data->point.y =
122:         LV_CLAMP(0,
123:                  data->point.y + (sample->y * CONFIG_LV_MOUSE_RATE),
124:                  ver_max);
125: 
126:     if(mouse_buttons & MOUSE_BUTTON_1 || mouse_buttons & MOUSE_BUTTON_2 ||
127:        mouse_buttons & MOUSE_BUTTON_3) {
128:         mouse->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
129:     }
130:     else {
131:         mouse->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
132:     }
133: }
134: 
135: static void mouse_read(lv_indev_t * drv, lv_indev_data_t * data)
136: {
137:     lv_nuttx_mouse_t * mouse = drv->driver_data;
138:     struct mouse_report_s sample;
139: 
140:     /*
141:      * Note: Since it is necessary to avoid multi-processing click events
142:      * caused by redundant continue_reading, a two-unit sample sliding window
143:      * algorithm is used here. continue_reading is only activated when there
144:      * are two points in the window.
145:      */
146: 
147:     /* If has last sample, use it first */
148:     if(mouse->has_last_sample) {
149:         conv_mouse_sample(drv, data, &mouse->last_sample);
150:     }
151:     else {
152:         /* Read first sample */
153:         if(!mouse_read_sample(mouse->fd, &sample)) {
154:             /* No sample available, return last state */
155:             data->state = mouse->last_state;
156:             return;
157:         }
158: 
159:         conv_mouse_sample(drv, data, &sample);
160:     }
161: 
162:     /* Try to read next sample */
163:     if(mouse_read_sample(mouse->fd, &sample)) {
164:         /* Save last sample and let lvgl continue reading */
165:         mouse->last_sample = sample;
166:         mouse->has_last_sample = true;
167:         data->continue_reading = true;
168:     }
169:     else {
170:         /* No more sample available, clear last sample flag */
171:         mouse->has_last_sample = false;
172:     }
173: 
174:     data->state = mouse->last_state;
175: }
176: 
177: static void mouse_delete_cb(lv_event_t * e)
178: {
179:     lv_indev_t * indev = (lv_indev_t *) lv_event_get_user_data(e);
180:     lv_nuttx_mouse_t * mouse = lv_indev_get_driver_data(indev);
181:     if(mouse) {
182:         lv_indev_set_driver_data(indev, NULL);
183:         lv_indev_set_read_cb(indev, NULL);
184:         mouse_set_cursor(indev, -1);
185: 
186:         if(mouse->fd >= 0) {
187:             close(mouse->fd);
188:             mouse->fd = -1;
189:         }
190:         lv_free(mouse);
191:         LV_LOG_USER("done");
192:     }
193: }
194: 
195: static void mouse_set_cursor(lv_indev_t * indev, int32_t size)
196: {
197:     lv_obj_t * cursor_obj = lv_indev_get_cursor(indev);
198:     if(size <= 0) {
199:         if(cursor_obj) {
200:             lv_obj_delete(cursor_obj);
201:             lv_indev_set_cursor(indev, NULL);
202:         }
203:     }
204:     else {
205:         if(cursor_obj == NULL) {
206:             cursor_obj = lv_obj_create(lv_layer_sys());
207:             lv_obj_remove_style_all(cursor_obj);
208:             lv_obj_set_style_radius(cursor_obj, LV_RADIUS_CIRCLE, 0);
209:             lv_obj_set_style_bg_opa(cursor_obj, LV_OPA_50, 0);
210:             lv_obj_set_style_bg_color(cursor_obj, lv_color_black(), 0);
211:             lv_obj_set_style_border_width(cursor_obj, 2, 0);
212:             lv_obj_set_style_border_color(cursor_obj, lv_palette_main(LV_PALETTE_GREY), 0);
213:         }
214:         lv_obj_set_size(cursor_obj, size, size);
215:         lv_obj_set_style_translate_x(cursor_obj, -size / 2, 0);
216:         lv_obj_set_style_translate_y(cursor_obj, -size / 2, 0);
217:         lv_indev_set_cursor(indev, cursor_obj);
218:     }
219: }
220: 
221: static lv_indev_t * mouse_init(int fd)
222: {
223:     lv_nuttx_mouse_t * mouse;
224:     lv_indev_t * indev = NULL;
225: 
226:     mouse = lv_malloc_zeroed(sizeof(lv_nuttx_mouse_t));
227:     if(mouse == NULL) {
228:         LV_LOG_ERROR("mouse_s malloc failed");
229:         return NULL;
230:     }
231: 
232:     mouse->fd = fd;
233:     mouse->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
234:     indev = lv_indev_create();
235: 
236:     if(indev == NULL) {
237:         LV_LOG_ERROR("indev create failed");
238:         lv_free(mouse);
239:         return NULL;

242:     lv_indev_set_type(indev, LV_INDEV_TYPE_POINTER);
243:     lv_indev_set_read_cb(indev, mouse_read);
244:     lv_indev_set_driver_data(indev, mouse);
245:     lv_indev_add_event_cb(indev, mouse_delete_cb, LV_EVENT_DELETE, indev);
246: 
247:     /* Set cursor icon */
248:     mouse_set_cursor(indev, 20);

76: int main(int argc, FAR char *argv[])
77: {
78: #ifdef CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_MOUSE
79:   struct mouse_report_s sample;
80: #else
81:   struct touch_sample_s sample;
82: #endif
83:   ssize_t nbytes;
84:   long nsamples;
85:   int fd;
86:   int errval = 0;
87: 
88:   /* If this example is configured as an NX add-on, then limit the number of
89:    * samples that we collect before returning.  Otherwise, we never return
90:    */
91: 
92:   nsamples = CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_NSAMPLES;
93:   if (argc > 1)
94:     {
95:       nsamples = strtol(argv[1], NULL, 10);
96:     }
97: 
98:   printf("tc_main: nsamples: %ld\n", nsamples);
99: 
100:   /* Open the touchscreen device for reading */
101: 
102:   printf("tc_main: Opening %s\n", CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_DEVPATH);
103:   fd = open(CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_DEVPATH, O_RDONLY);
104:   if (fd < 0)
105:     {
106:       printf("tc_main: open %s failed: %d\n",
107:               CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_DEVPATH, errno);
108:       errval = 2;
109:       goto errout;
110:     }
111: 
112:   /* Now loop the appropriate number of times, displaying the collected
113:    * touchscreen samples.
114:    */
115: 
116:   for (; ; )
117:     {
118:       /* Flush any output before the loop entered or from the previous pass
119:        * through the loop.
120:        */
121: 
122:       fflush(stdout);
123: 
124: #ifdef CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_MOUSE
125:       /* Read one sample */
126: 
127:       iinfo("Reading...\n");
128:       nbytes = read(fd, &sample, sizeof(struct mouse_report_s));
129:       iinfo("Bytes read: %zd\n", nbytes);
130: 
131:       /* Handle unexpected return values */
132: 
133:       if (nbytes < 0)
134:         {
135:           errval = errno;
136:           if (errval != EINTR)
137:             {
138:               printf("tc_main: read %s failed: %d\n",
139:                      CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_DEVPATH, errval);
140:               errval = 3;
141:               goto errout_with_dev;
142:             }
143: 
144:           printf("tc_main: Interrupted read...\n");
145:         }
146:       else if (nbytes != sizeof(struct mouse_report_s))
147:         {
148:           printf("tc_main: Unexpected read size=%zd,expected=%zd,Ignoring\n",
149:                  nbytes, sizeof(struct mouse_report_s));
150:         }
151: 
152:       /* Print the sample data on successful return */
153: 
154:       else
155:         {
156:           printf("Sample     :\n");
157:           printf("   buttons : %02x\n", sample.buttons);
158:           printf("         x : %d\n",   sample.x);
159:           printf("         y : %d\n",   sample.y);
160: #ifdef CONFIG_INPUT_MOUSE_WHEEL
161:           printf("     wheel : %d\n",   sample.wheel);
162: #endif
163:         }
164: #else
165:       /* Read one sample */
166: 
167:       iinfo("Reading...\n");
168:       nbytes = read(fd, &sample, sizeof(struct touch_sample_s));
169:       iinfo("Bytes read: %zd\n", nbytes);
170: 
171:       /* Handle unexpected return values */
172: 
173:       if (nbytes < 0)
174:         {
175:           errval = errno;
176:           if (errval != EINTR)
177:             {
178:               printf("tc_main: read %s failed: %d\n",
179:                      CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TOUCHSCREEN_DEVPATH, errval);
180:               errval = 3;
181:               goto errout_with_dev;
182:             }
183: 
184:           printf("tc_main: Interrupted read...\n");
185:         }
186:       else if (nbytes != sizeof(struct touch_sample_s))
187:         {
188:           printf("tc_main: Unexpected read size=%zd, expected=%zd, "
189:                  "Ignoring\n",
190:                  nbytes, sizeof(struct touch_sample_s));
191:         }
192: 
193:       /* Print the sample data on successful return */
194: 
195:       else
196:         {
197:           printf("Sample     :\n");
198:           printf("   npoints : %"PRId32"\n",   sample.npoints);
199:           printf("Point 1    :\n");
200:           printf("        id : %d\n",   sample.point[0].id);
201:           printf("     flags : %02x\n", sample.point[0].flags);
202:           printf("         x : %d\n",   sample.point[0].x);
203:           printf("         y : %d\n",   sample.point[0].y);
204:           printf("         h : %d\n",   sample.point[0].h);
205:           printf("         w : %d\n",   sample.point[0].w);
206:           printf("  pressure : %d\n",   sample.point[0].pressure);
207:           printf(" timestamp : %" PRIu64"\n", sample.point[0].timestamp);
208:         }
209: #endif
210: 
211:       if (nsamples && --nsamples <= 0)
212:         {
213:           break;
214:         }
215:     }
216: 
217: errout_with_dev:
218:   close(fd);
219: 
220: errout:
221:   printf("Terminating!\n");
222:   fflush(stdout);
223:   return errval;
224: }

51: struct input_device_s;

93: /****************************************************************************
94:  * Name: open_device
95:  ****************************************************************************/
96: 
97: static int open_device(FAR struct input_device_s *dev)
98: {
99:   GETEVENT_INFO("opening %s\n", dev->path);
100:   dev->fd = open(dev->path, O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC);
101: 
102:   if (dev->fd < 0)
103:     {
104:       GETEVENT_INFO("open %s failed, errno: %d\n", dev->path, errno);
105:       return -errno;
106:     }
107: 
108:   if (dev->init_cb)
109:     {
110:       return dev->init_cb(dev);
111:     }
112: 
113:   return 0;
114: }

117:  * Name: touch_init
118:  ****************************************************************************/

120: static int touch_init(FAR struct input_device_s *dev)
121: {
122:   FAR struct touch_priv_s *priv;
123:   uint8_t maxpoint;
124:   int ret;
125: 
126:   ret = ioctl(dev->fd, TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS, &maxpoint);
127:   if (ret < 0)
128:     {
129:       GETEVENT_INFO("ioctl GETMAXPOINTS failed: %d, "
130:                     "errno: %d\n", ret, errno);
131:       return -errno;
132:     }
133: 
134:   priv = calloc(1, sizeof(struct touch_priv_s) +
135:                 SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(maxpoint));
136:   if (!priv)
137:     {
138:       GETEVENT_INFO("Memory allocation failed for touch_priv_s\n");
139:       return -ENOMEM;
140:     }
141: 
142:   priv->maxpoint = maxpoint;
143:   dev->priv = priv;
144:   GETEVENT_INFO("ioctl TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS: %d\n", maxpoint);
145:   return ret;
146: }

150:  ****************************************************************************/

153: {
154:   struct mouse_report_s sample;
155:   ssize_t nbytes;
156: 
157:   /* Read one sample */
158: 
159:   nbytes = read(dev->fd, &sample, sizeof(struct mouse_report_s));
160: 
161:   /* Print the sample data on successful return */
162: 
163:   if (nbytes == sizeof(struct mouse_report_s))
164:     {
165:       GETEVENT_INFO("mouse event: %s\n", dev->path);
166:       GETEVENT_INFO("   buttons : %02" PRIx8 "\n", sample.buttons);
167:       GETEVENT_INFO("         x : %d\n", sample.x);
168:       GETEVENT_INFO("         y : %d\n", sample.y);
169: #ifdef CONFIG_INPUT_MOUSE_WHEEL
170:       GETEVENT_INFO("     wheel : %d\n", sample.wheel);
171: #endif
172:     }
173: }

176:  * Name: read_touch_event
177:  ****************************************************************************/
178: 
179: static void read_touch_event(FAR struct input_device_s *dev)
180: {
181:   FAR struct touch_priv_s *priv = (FAR struct touch_priv_s *)dev->priv;
182:   ssize_t nbytes;
183:   size_t i;
184: 
185:   /* Read one sample */
186: 
187:   nbytes = read(dev->fd, priv->sample,
188:                 SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(priv->maxpoint));
189: 
190:   /* Print the sample data on successful return */
191: 
192:   if (nbytes == SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(priv->maxpoint))
193:     {
194:       GETEVENT_INFO("touch event: %s\n", dev->path);
195:       GETEVENT_INFO("   npoints : %" PRId32 "\n", priv->sample->npoints);
196:       for (i = 0; i < priv->maxpoint; i++)
197:         {
198:           if (priv->sample->point[i].flags == 0)
199:             {
200:               break;
201:             }
202: 
203:           GETEVENT_INFO("Point      : %d\n", priv->sample->point[i].id);
204:           GETEVENT_INFO("     flags : %02x\n", priv->sample->point[i].flags);
205:           GETEVENT_INFO("         x : %d\n", priv->sample->point[i].x);
206:           GETEVENT_INFO("         y : %d\n", priv->sample->point[i].y);
207: #ifdef CONFIG_GRAPHICS_INPUT_GETEVENT_DETAIL_INFO
208:           GETEVENT_INFO("         h : %d\n", priv->sample->point[i].h);
209:           GETEVENT_INFO("         w : %d\n", priv->sample->point[i].w);
210:           GETEVENT_INFO("  pressure : %d\n",
211:                         priv->sample->point[i].pressure);
212: #endif
213:           GETEVENT_INFO(" timestamp : %" PRIu64"\n",
214:                         priv->sample->point[i].timestamp);
215:         }
216:     }
217: }

227:

229:

233: 
234:   if (nbytes == sizeof(struct keyboard_event_s))
235:     {
236:       GETEVENT_INFO("keyboard event: %s\n", dev->path);
237:       GETEVENT_INFO("         type : %" PRIu32 "\n", sample.type);

242: /****************************************************************************
243:  * Name: cleanup_input_devices
244:  ****************************************************************************/
245: 
246: static void cleanup_input_devices(FAR struct input_devices_ctx_s *ctx)
247: {
248:   FAR struct input_device_s *dev = ctx->head;
249:   FAR struct input_device_s *next;
250: 
251:   while (dev)

280:  ****************************************************************************/
281: 
282: static void run_event_loop(FAR struct input_devices_ctx_s *ctx)
283: {
284:   FAR struct input_device_s *dev;
285:   FAR struct pollfd *fds = NULL;
286:   volatile sig_atomic_t running = 1;
287:   struct sigaction sa;
288:   int fd_count = 0;
289:   int timeout = 500;
290:   int i = 0;
291:   int ret;
292: 
293:   sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO;
294:   sa.sa_sigaction = signal_handler;
295:   sigemptyset(&sa.sa_mask);
296:   sa.sa_user = (FAR void *)&running;
297:   sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
298: 
299:   for (dev = ctx->head; dev; dev = dev->next)
300:     {
301:       if (dev->fd >= 0)
302:         {
303:           fd_count++;
304:         }
305:     }
306: 
307:   fds = calloc(fd_count, sizeof(struct pollfd));
308: 
309:   if (!fds)
310:     {
311:       GETEVENT_INFO("Memory allocation failed for fds\n");
312:       return;
313:     }
314: 
315:   for (dev = ctx->head; dev; dev = dev->next)
316:     {
317:       if (dev->fd >= 0)
318:         {
319:           fds[i].fd = dev->fd;
320:           fds[i].events = POLLIN;
321:           fds[i].revents = 0;
322:           i++;
323:         }
324:     }
325: 
326:   while (running)
327:     {
328:       ret = poll(fds, fd_count, timeout);
329:       if (ret < 0 && errno != EINTR)
330:         {
331:           GETEVENT_INFO("poll error: %d\n", errno);
332:           break;
333:         }
334: 
335:       for (i = 0; i < fd_count; i++)
336:         {
337:           if (!(fds[i].revents & POLLIN))
338:             {
339:               continue;
340:             }
341: 
342:           for (dev = ctx->head; dev; dev = dev->next)
343:             {
344:               if (dev->fd == fds[i].fd)
345:                 {
346:                   dev->read_cb(dev);
347:                   break;
348:                 }
349:             }
350:         }
351:     }
352: 
353:   free(fds);
354: }

435:  ****************************************************************************/
436: 
437: static int detect_devices(FAR struct input_devices_ctx_s *ctx)
438: {
439:   FAR struct dirent *entry;
440:   char path[PATH_MAX];
441:   FAR DIR *dir;
442:   int ret = 0;
443: 
444:   dir = opendir("/dev");
445:   if (!dir)
446:     {
447:       GETEVENT_INFO("Failed to open /dev directory, errno: %d\n", errno);
448:       return -errno;
449:     }
450: 
451:   while ((entry = readdir(dir)))
452:     {
453:       if (entry->d_type == DT_CHR)
454:         {
455:           if (snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/dev/%s", entry->d_name) < 0)
456:             {
457:               GETEVENT_INFO("Memory allocation failed for path\n");
458:               continue;
459:             }
460: 
461:           if (strncmp(entry->d_name, "mouse", 5) == 0)
462:             {
463:               ret = add_input_device(ctx, NULL, read_mouse_event, path);
464:             }
465:           else if (strncmp(entry->d_name, "input", 5) == 0)
466:             {

468:                                      path);
469:             }
470:           else if (strncmp(entry->d_name, "kbd", 3) == 0)
471:             {
472:               ret = add_input_device(ctx, NULL, read_keyboard_event, path);
473:             }
474: 
475:           if (ret < 0)
476:             {
477:               break;
478:             }
479:         }
480:     }

483:   return ret;

519:         }

1: # Input Event Monitor - getevent
2: 
3: ## Features
4: - 🖱️ Mouse event monitoring (clicks/movement/wheel)
5: - 👆 Multi-touch event capture (coordinates/pressure/timestamps)
6: - ⌨️ Keyboard key press detection (key codes/event types)
7: - 🔍 Automatic input device detection in `/dev`
8: - ⚙️ Command-line device path specification
9: - 🚦 Non-blocking I/O with 500ms timeout
10: - 🔒 Resource-safe memory management
11: 
12: ## Build Configuration
13: Enable in NuttX configuration:
14: ```bash
15: # Enable getevent utility
16: CONFIG_GRAPHICS_INPUT_GETEVENT=y
17: 
18: # Optional debug details (requires recompilation)
19: CONFIG_GRAPHICS_INPUT_GETEVENT_DETAIL_INFO=y
20: ```
21: 
22: ## Usage
23: ```bash
24: # Auto-detect all input devices
25: getevent
26: 
27: # Monitor specific mouse device
28: getevent -m /dev/mouse0
29: 
30: # Monitor specific touch device
31: getevent -t /dev/input0
32: 
33: # Monitor specific keyboard
34: getevent -k /dev/kbd0
35: 
36: # Combine multiple devices
37: getevent -m /dev/mouse0 -t /dev/input0
38: ```
39: 
40: ## Requirements
41: 
42: ### NuttX Input Subsystem
43: The application is built with NuttX input subsystem support, which is required for input event handling.
44: 
45: ### Kernel Syslog Output
46: The kernel must be configured to output syslog messages for enhanced debugging capabilities.
47: 
48: ### Termination
49: Press `Ctrl+C` to safely terminate the monitoring process.

113: static int touch_open(FAR struct file *filep)
114: {
115:   FAR struct touch_openpriv_s  *openpriv;
116:   FAR struct inode             *inode = filep->f_inode;
117:   FAR struct touch_upperhalf_s *upper = inode->i_private;
118:   FAR struct touch_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
119:   irqstate_t flags;
120:   int ret;
121: 
122:   openpriv = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct touch_openpriv_s));
123:   if (openpriv == NULL)
124:     {
125:       return -ENOMEM;
126:     }
127: 
128:   ret = circbuf_init(&openpriv->circbuf, NULL,
129:                      upper->nums * SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(lower->maxpoint));
130:   if (ret < 0)
131:     {
132:       kmm_free(openpriv);
133:       return ret;
134:     }
135: 
136:   nxsem_init(&openpriv->waitsem, 0, 0);
137:   spin_lock_init(&openpriv->lock);
138: 
139:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&upper->lock);
140:   list_add_tail(&upper->head, &openpriv->node);
141:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&upper->lock, flags);
142: 
143:   /* Save the buffer node pointer so that it can be used directly
144:    * in the read operation.
145:    */
146: 
147:   filep->f_priv = openpriv;
148: 
149:   return ret;
150: }

157: {
158:   FAR struct touch_openpriv_s  *openpriv = filep->f_priv;
159:   FAR struct inode             *inode    = filep->f_inode;
160:   FAR struct touch_upperhalf_s *upper    = inode->i_private;
161:   irqstate_t flags;
162: 
163:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&upper->lock);
164: 
165:   if (upper->grab == openpriv)
166:     {
167:       upper->grab = NULL;
168:     }
169: 
170:   list_delete(&openpriv->node);
171:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&upper->lock, flags);
172: 
173:   circbuf_uninit(&openpriv->circbuf);
174:   nxsem_destroy(&openpriv->waitsem);
175:   kmm_free(openpriv);

188:   FAR struct touch_upperhalf_s *upper = inode->i_private;

203: static ssize_t touch_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
204:                           size_t len)
205: {
206:   FAR struct touch_openpriv_s *openpriv = filep->f_priv;
207:   irqstate_t flags;
208:   int ret;
209: 
210:   if (!buffer || !len)
211:     {
212:       return -EINVAL;
213:     }

215:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&openpriv->lock);
216:

228:           if (ret < 0)
229:             {

231:             }
232: 
233:           flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&openpriv->lock);
234:         }
235:     }
236:

238:

241:   return ret;
242: }

248: static int touch_ioctl(FAR struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg)
249: {
250:   FAR struct touch_openpriv_s  *openpriv = filep->f_priv;
251:   FAR struct inode             *inode    = filep->f_inode;
252:   FAR struct touch_upperhalf_s *upper    = inode->i_private;
253:   FAR struct touch_lowerhalf_s *lower    = upper->lower;
254:   irqstate_t flags;
255:   int ret = OK;
256: 
257:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&upper->lock);
258: 
259:   switch (cmd)
260:     {
261:       case TSIOC_GRAB:
262:         {
263:           int enable = (int)arg;
264:           if (enable)
265:             {
266:               if (upper->grab != NULL)
267:                 {
268:                   ret = -EBUSY;
269:                 }
270:               else
271:                 {
272:                   upper->grab = openpriv;
273:                 }
274:             }
275:           else
276:             {
277:               if (upper->grab != openpriv)
278:                 {
279:                   ret = -EINVAL;
280:                 }
281:               else
282:                 {
283:                   upper->grab = NULL;
284:                 }
285:             }
286:         }
287:         break;
288:       case TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS:
289:         {
290:           if (arg == 0)
291:             {
292:               ret = -EINVAL;
293:               break;
294:             }
295: 
296:           FAR uint8_t *ptr = (FAR uint8_t *)((uintptr_t)arg);
297:           *ptr = lower->maxpoint;
298:         }
299:         break;
300:       default:
301:         {
302:           if (lower->control)
303:             {
304:               ret = lower->control(lower, cmd, arg);
305:             }
306:           else
307:             {
308:               ret = -ENOTTY;
309:             }
310:         }
311:         break;
312:     }
313: 
314:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&upper->lock, flags);
315:   return ret;
316: }

322: static int touch_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
323:                       bool setup)
324: {
325:   FAR struct touch_openpriv_s *openpriv = filep->f_priv;
326:   pollevent_t eventset = 0;
327:   irqstate_t flags;
328:   int ret = OK;
329: 
330:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt(&openpriv->lock);
331: 
332:   if (setup)
333:     {
334:       if (openpriv->fds == NULL)
335:         {
336:           openpriv->fds = fds;
337:           fds->priv     = &openpriv->fds;
338:         }
339:       else
340:         {
341:           ret = -EBUSY;
342:           goto errout;
343:         }
344: 
345:       if (!circbuf_is_empty(&openpriv->circbuf))
346:         {
347:           eventset |= POLLIN;
348:         }
349: 
350:       poll_notify(&fds, 1, eventset);
351:     }
352:   else if (fds->priv)
353:     {
354:       openpriv->fds = NULL;
355:       fds->priv     = NULL;
356:     }
357: 
358: errout:
359:   spin_unlock_irqrestore_nopreempt(&openpriv->lock, flags);
360:   return ret;
361: }

381:     }
382: 
383:   poll_notify(&openpriv->fds, 1, POLLIN);
384:   spin_unlock_irqrestore_nopreempt(&openpriv->lock, flags);
385: }

1: # contest2026_349_board（VSAI LogicPi A1）
2: 
3: 映射到 openvela `vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_349_board`，为
4: VSAI LogicPi A1（Amlogic Meson S6，Cortex-A55，GICv3）提供板级适配。
5: 
6: ## 分仓说明
7: 
8: 本仓只包含板级适配。芯片级支持在独立的 nuttx 分仓，本项目必须配合
9: 它编译：
10: 
11: - <https://github.com/U2FsdGVkX1/vela-nuttx>（`dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支，
12:   基于 `open-vela/nuttx` 同名分支）
13: 
14: `repo sync` 得到的 `nuttx/` 不含芯片支持，编译前需把工作区 `nuttx/`
15: 切换到上述分仓：
16: 
17: ```bash
18: cd <openvela 工作区>/nuttx
19: git remote add fork https://github.com/U2FsdGVkX1/vela-nuttx.git
20: git fetch fork dev-ai-contest-2026
21: git checkout -B dev-ai-contest-2026 FETCH_HEAD
22: ```
23: 
24: ## 硬件
25: 
26: - 底板初始化（DDR/时钟/pinmux）由 BL31/U-Boot 完成，NuttX 从
27:   `0x03080000` 启动（U-Boot `booti` 重定位后的地址）。
28: - 控制台：UART0，921600 波特。
29: 
30: ## 构建
31: 
32: 在 openvela 工作区根目录执行：
33: 
34: ```bash
35: ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_349_board/configs/nsh -j    # NSH 基线
36: ```
37: 
38: 部署：U-Boot 将 `nuttx.bin` 读到 `0x03080000` 后 `booti`。

## 2. 内存布局：从 U-Boot 源码确认了低区保留，上界还差一个数据

已确认（`android_multidisplay.env` + `s6_bq201.h`）：

| 地址 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `0x00080000` | `loadaddr_rtos`（Amlogic RTOS） |
| `0x00300000` | U-Boot logo framebuffer（`fb_addr`） |
| `0x01000000` | dtb（`dtb_mem_addr`） |
| `0x01080000` | 通用 `loadaddr` |
| **`0x03000000`** | **`loadaddr_kernel` —— Amlogic 自家内核加载地址，NuttX 选这里完全对齐平台惯例** |
| DRAM 顶端 | `SYS_MEM_TOP_HIDE 8MB` + `BL32_SHARE_MEM 8MB`（安全侧保留） |

即 `0x03000000` 以下全部是引导链保留区，你们现有 RAM_START 正确；DDR 总量由 BL2 自动探测（env 里 `ddr_size=0` = auto），**repo 里查不到 LogicPi A1 实际容量和 ATF/secmon 的确切位置**。

建议：下次上板在 U-Boot 命令行跑一下 `bdinfo`，把 `ram_size`/`ram_top` 发我，就能定 `RAM_SIZE` 上限。保守方案先按 0x03000000–0x05000000（32MB）做：双 fb 16.6MB + LVGL 缓冲 + 堆 ≈ 20MB，够用。"}

258: static void launcher_paint_dot(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t r)
259: {
260:   int32_t dx;
261:   int32_t dy;
262:   int32_t w = LAUNCHER_SCREEN_W;
263:   int32_t h = LAUNCHER_SCREEN_H;
264: 
265:   for (dy = -r; dy <= r; dy++)
266:     {
267:       for (dx = -r; dx <= r; dx++)
268:         {
269:           if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= r * r &&
270:               x + dx >= 0 && x + dx < w && y + dy >= 0 && y + dy < h)
271:             {
272:               g_canvas_buf[(y + dy) * w + (x + dx)] = g_brush_color;
273:             }
274:         }
275:     }
276: }
277: 
278: static void launcher_paint_stroke(int32_t x0, int32_t y0,
279:                                   int32_t x1, int32_t y1)
280: {
281:   int32_t dx = x1 - x0;
282:   int32_t dy = y1 - y0;
283:   int32_t steps = abs(dx) > abs(dy) ? abs(dx) : abs(dy);
284:   int32_t i;
285: 
286:   if (steps == 0)
287:     {
288:       launcher_paint_dot(x1, y1, 6);
289:       return;
290:     }
291: 
292:   for (i = 0; i <= steps; i += 4)
293:     {
294:       launcher_paint_dot(x0 + dx * i / steps, y0 + dy * i / steps, 6);
295:     }
296: }

87:         LV_LOG_ERROR("get touch maxpoints failed (errno=%d)", errno);

94:         close(fd);
95:         return NULL;

98:     LV_LOG_USER("touchscreen %s open success, maxpoint %d", dev_path, maxpoint);
99: 
100:     indev = touchscreen_init(fd, maxpoint);
101: 
102:     if(indev == NULL) {
103:         close(fd);
104:         return NULL;

142: static void process_single_touch(lv_indev_t * drv,
143:                                  lv_indev_data_t * data,
144:                                  struct touch_sample_s * sample)
145: {
146:     lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen = drv->driver_data;
147:     uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[0].flags;
148: 
149:     if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
150:         lv_display_t * disp = lv_indev_get_display(drv);
151:         int32_t hor_max = lv_display_get_horizontal_resolution(disp) - 1;
152:         int32_t ver_max = lv_display_get_vertical_resolution(disp) - 1;
153: 
154:         data->point.x = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[0].x, hor_max);
155:         data->point.y = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[0].y, ver_max);
156:         touchscreen->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
157: 
158:         if(touch_flags & TOUCH_DOWN) {
159:             touchscreen->primary_point.id = sample->point[0].id;
160:             touchscreen->primary_point.x = data->point.x;
161:             touchscreen->primary_point.y = data->point.y;
162:         }
163:     }
164:     else if(touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) {
165:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
166:         touchscreen->last_state = LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED;
167:     }
168: }

170: #if LV_USE_GESTURE_RECOGNITION
171: static void touchscreen_update_primary_point(struct touch_sample_s * sample,
172:                                              lv_nuttx_touchscreen_t * touchscreen,
173:                                              int32_t hor_max, int32_t ver_max)
174: {
175:     int primary_index = -1;
176: 
177:     for(int i = 0; i < sample->npoints; i++) {
178:         uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[i].flags;
179: 
180:         if(touchscreen->primary_point.id == sample->point[i].id) {
181:             if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
182:                 primary_index = i;
183:                 break;
184:             }
185:             else if((touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) && primary_index >= 0) {
186:                 break;
187:             }
188:         }
189:         else if((touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) && primary_index < 0) {
190:             primary_index = i;
191:         }
192:     }
193: 
194:     if(primary_index != -1) {
195:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = sample->point[primary_index].id;
196:         touchscreen->primary_point.x =
197:             LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[primary_index].x, hor_max);
198:         touchscreen->primary_point.y =
199:             LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[primary_index].y, ver_max);
200:     }
201:     else {
202:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
203:     }

211:     lv_indev_touch_data_t * touch_data_tmp = touchscreen->touch_data;
212:     lv_display_t * disp = lv_indev_get_display(indev);
213:     int32_t hor_max = lv_display_get_horizontal_resolution(disp) - 1;
214:     int32_t ver_max = lv_display_get_vertical_resolution(disp) - 1;
215:     uint16_t finger_release_cnt = 0;
216: 
217:     for(int i = 0; i < sample->npoints; i++) {
218:         touch_data_tmp->id = sample->point[i].id;
219:         uint8_t touch_flags = sample->point[i].flags;
220:         if(touch_flags & (TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_MOVE)) {
221:             touch_data_tmp->point.x = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[i].x, hor_max);
222:             touch_data_tmp->point.y = LV_CLAMP(0, sample->point[i].y, ver_max);
223:             touch_data_tmp->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
224:             touch_data_tmp++;

226:         else if(touch_flags & TOUCH_UP) {

238:     data->update_primary_point = false;

241:         touchscreen->primary_point.id = UINT8_MAX;
242:     }
243:     else {
244:         data->state = LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED;
245:         if(finger_release_cnt > 0) {

247:         }

249:         touchscreen_update_primary_point(sample, touchscreen, hor_max, ver_max);

143: /****************************************************************************
144:  * Name: gt9xx_i2c_read
145:  *
146:  * Description:
147:  *   Read a Touch Panel Register over I2C.
148:  *
149:  * Input Parameters:
150:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
151:  *   reg    - I2C Register to be read
152:  *   buf    - Receive Buffer
153:  *   buflen - Number of bytes to be read
154:  *
155:  * Returned Value:
156:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
157:  *
158:  ****************************************************************************/
159: 
160: static int gt9xx_i2c_read(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
161:                           uint16_t reg,
162:                           uint8_t *buf,
163:                           size_t buflen)
164: {
165:   int ret;
166: 
167:   /* Send the Register Address, MSB first */
168: 
169:   uint8_t regbuf[2] =
170:   {
171:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
172:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
173:   };
174: 
175:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
176: 
177:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
178:   {
179:     {
180:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
181: 
182:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
183:       .addr      = dev->addr,
184:       .flags     = 0,
185:       .buffer    = regbuf,
186:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
187:     },
188:     {
189:       /* Receive the I2C Register Values */
190: 
191:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
192:       .addr      = dev->addr,
193:       .flags     = I2C_M_READ,
194:       .buffer    = buf,
195:       .length    = buflen
196:     }
197:   };
198: 
199:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
200: 
201:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, buflen=%ld\n", reg, buflen);
202:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c && buf);
203: 
204:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
205: 
206:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
207:   if (ret < 0)
208:     {
209:       ierr("I2C Read failed: %d\n", ret);
210:       return ret;
211:     }
212: 
213: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO
214:   iinfodumpbuffer("gt9xx_i2c_read", buf, buflen);
215: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO */
216: 
217:   return OK;
218: }

228:  *   reg - I2C Register to be written

246:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
247:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
248:   };
249: 
250:   /* Send the Register Value */
251: 
252:   uint8_t buf[1] =
253:   {
254:     val  /* Value to be written */
255:   };
256: 
257:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
258: 
259:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
260:   {
261:     {
262:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
263: 
264:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
265:       .addr      = dev->addr,
266:       .flags     = 0,
267:       .buffer    = regbuf,
268:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
269:     },
270:     {
271:       /* Send the I2C Register Value */
272: 
273:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
274:       .addr      = dev->addr,
275:       .flags     = I2C_M_NOSTART,
276:       .buffer    = buf,
277:       .length    = sizeof(buf)
278:     }
279:   };
280: 
281:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
282: 
283:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, val=%d\n", reg, val);
284:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c);
285: 
286:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
287: 
288:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
289:   if (ret < 0)
290:     {
291:       ierr("I2C Write failed: %d\n", ret);
292:       return ret;
293:     }
294: 
295:   return OK;
296: }

369: /****************************************************************************
370:  * Name: gt9xx_read_touch_data
371:  *
372:  * Description:
373:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
374:  *   Touch Points.
375:  *
376:  * Input Parameters:
377:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
378:  *   sample - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
379:  *
380:  * Returned Value:
381:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
382:  *
383:  ****************************************************************************/
384: 
385: static int gt9xx_read_touch_data(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
386:                                  FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample)
387: {
388:   uint8_t status[1];
389:   uint8_t status_code;
390:   uint8_t touched_points;
391:   uint8_t touch[6];
392:   uint16_t x;
393:   uint16_t y;
394:   uint8_t flags;
395:   int ret;
396: 
397:   /* Erase the Touch Sample and Touch Point */
398: 
399:   iinfo("\n");
400:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && sample);
401:   memset(sample, 0, sizeof(*sample));
402: 
403:   /* Read the Touch Panel Status */
404: 
405:   ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_READ_COOR_ADDR, status, sizeof(status));
406:   if (ret < 0)
407:     {
408:       ierr("Read Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
409:       return ret;
410:     }
411: 
412:   /* Decode the Status Code and the Touched Points */
413: 
414:   status_code = status[0] & 0x80;
415:   touched_points = status[0] & 0x0f;
416: 
417:   /* If Touch Panel Status is OK and Touched Points is 1 or more */
418: 
419:   if (status_code != 0 && touched_points >= 1)
420:     {
421:       /* Read the First Touch Point (6 bytes) */
422: 
423:       ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_POINT1, touch, sizeof(touch));
424:       if (ret < 0)
425:         {
426:           ierr("Read Touch Point failed: %d\n", ret);
427:           return ret;
428:         }
429: 
430:       /* Decode the Touch Coordinates */
431: 
432:       x = touch[0] + (touch[1] << 8);
433:       y = touch[2] + (touch[3] << 8);
434: 
435:       /* Return the Touch Coordinates as Touch Down */
436: 
437:       flags = TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
438:       sample->npoints = 1;
439:       sample->point[0].id = 0;
440:       sample->point[0].x = x;
441:       sample->point[0].y = y;
442:       sample->point[0].flags = flags;
443:       iinfo("touch down x=%d, y=%d\n", x, y);
444:     }
445: 
446:   /* Set the Touch Panel Status to 0 */
447: 
448:   ret = gt9xx_set_status(dev, 0);
449:   if (ret < 0)
450:     {
451:       ierr("Set Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
452:       return ret;
453:     }
454: 
455:   return OK;
456: }

458: /****************************************************************************
459:  * Name: gt9xx_read
460:  *
461:  * Description:
462:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
463:  *   Touch Points.
464:  *
465:  * Input Parameters:
466:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
467:  *   buffer - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
468:  *   buflen - Size of buffer
469:  *
470:  * Returned Value:
471:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
472:  *
473:  ****************************************************************************/
474: 
475: static ssize_t gt9xx_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
476:                           size_t buflen)
477: {
478:   FAR struct inode *inode;
479:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
480:   struct touch_sample_s sample;
481:   const size_t outlen = sizeof(sample);
482:   irqstate_t flags;
483:   int ret;
484: 
485:   /* Returned Touch Sample will have 0 or 1 Touch Points */
486: 
487:   iinfo("buflen=%ld\n", buflen);
488:   if (buflen < outlen)
489:     {
490:       ierr("Buffer should be at least %ld bytes, got %ld bytes\n",
491:            outlen, buflen);
492:       return -EINVAL;
493:     }
494: 
495:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
496: 
497:   inode = filep->f_inode;
498:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
499:   priv = inode->i_private;
500: 
501:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent reads */
502: 
503:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
504:   if (ret < 0)
505:     {
506:       return ret;
507:     }
508: 
509:   ret = -EINVAL;
510: 
511:   /* If waiting for Touch Up, return the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
512: 
513:   if (priv->flags & TOUCH_DOWN)
514:     {
515:       /* Begin Critical Section */
516: 
517:       flags = enter_critical_section();
518: 
519:       /* Mark the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
520: 
521:       priv->flags = TOUCH_UP | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
522: 
523:       /* End Critical Section */
524: 
525:       leave_critical_section(flags);
526: 
527:       /* Return the Last Touch Point, changed to Touch Up */
528: 
529:       memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
530:       sample.npoints = 1;
531:       sample.point[0].id = 0;
532:       sample.point[0].x = priv->x;
533:       sample.point[0].y = priv->y;
534:       sample.point[0].flags = priv->flags;
535:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
536:       ret = OK;
537:       iinfo("touch up x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
538:     }
539:   else
540:     {
541:       /* Otherwise read the Touch Point over I2C */
542: 
543:       ret = gt9xx_read_touch_data(priv, &sample);
544: 
545:       /* Skip duplicates */
546: 
547:       if (sample.npoints >= 1 &&
548:           priv->x == sample.point[0].x &&
549:           priv->y == sample.point[0].y)
550:         {
551:           memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
552:           sample.npoints = 0;
553:           iinfo("skip duplicate x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
554:         }
555: 
556:       /* Return the Touch Point */
557: 
558:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
559: 
560:       /* Begin Critical Section */
561: 
562:       flags = enter_critical_section();
563: 
564:       /* Clear the Interrupt Pending Flag */
565: 
566:       priv->int_pending = false;
567: 
568:       /* Remember the Last Touch Point */
569: 
570:       if (sample.npoints >= 1)
571:         {
572:           priv->x = sample.point[0].x;
573:           priv->y = sample.point[0].y;
574:           priv->flags = sample.point[0].flags;
575:         }
576: 
577:       /* End Critical Section */
578: 
579:       leave_critical_section(flags);
580:     }
581: 
582:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow next read */
583: 
584:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
585:   return (ret < 0) ? ret : outlen;
586: }

590:  *
591:  * Description:
592:  *   Open the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the first open, we power on
593:  *   the Touch Panel, probe for the Touch Panel and enable Touch Panel
594:  *   Interrupts.
595:  *
596:  * Input Parameters:
597:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
598:  *
599:  * Returned Value:
600:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
601:  *
602:  ****************************************************************************/
603: 
604: static int gt9xx_open(FAR struct file *filep)
605: {
606:   FAR struct inode *inode;
607:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
608:   unsigned int use_count;
609:   int ret;
610: 
611:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
612: 
613:   iinfo("\n");
614:   inode = filep->f_inode;
615:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
616:   priv = inode->i_private;
617: 
618:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
619: 
620:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
621:   if (ret < 0)
622:     {
623:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
624:       return ret;
625:     }
626: 
627:   /* Get next Reference Count */
628: 
629:   use_count = priv->cref + 1;
630:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count < UINT8_MAX && use_count > priv->cref);
631:   if (use_count == 1)
632:     {
633:       /* If first user, power on the Touch Panel */
634: 
635:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power != NULL);
636:       ret = priv->board->set_power(priv->board, true);
637:       if (ret < 0)
638:         {
639:           goto out_lock;
640:         }
641: 
642:       /* Let Touch Panel power up before probing */
643: 
644:       nxsig_usleep(100 * 1000);
645: 
646:       /* Check that Touch Panel exists on I2C */
647: 
648:       ret = gt9xx_probe_device(priv);
649:       if (ret < 0)
650:         {
651:           /* No such device, power off the Touch Panel */
652: 
653:           priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
654:           goto out_lock;
655:         }
656: 
657:       /* Enable Touch Panel Interrupts */
658: 
659:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
660:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, true);
661:     }
662: 
663:   /* Set the Reference Count */
664: 
665:   priv->cref = use_count;
666: 
667:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
668: 
669: out_lock:
670:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
671:   return ret;
672: }
673: 
674: /****************************************************************************
675:  * Name: gt9xx_close
676:  *
677:  * Description:
678:  *   Close the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the final close, we disable
679:  *   Touch Panel Interrupts and power off the Touch Panel.
680:  *
681:  * Input Parameters:
682:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
683:  *
684:  * Returned Value:
685:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
686:  *
687:  ****************************************************************************/
688: 
689: static int gt9xx_close(FAR struct file *filep)
690: {
691:   FAR struct inode *inode;
692:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
693:   int use_count;
694:   int ret;
695: 
696:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
697: 
698:   iinfo("\n");
699:   inode = filep->f_inode;
700:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
701:   priv = inode->i_private;
702: 
703:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
704: 
705:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
706:   if (ret < 0)
707:     {
708:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
709:       return ret;
710:     }
711: 
712:   /* Decrement the Reference Count */
713: 
714:   use_count = priv->cref - 1;
715:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count >= 0);
716:   if (use_count == 0)
717:     {
718:       /* If final user, disable Touch Panel Interrupts */
719: 
720:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board && priv->board->irq_enable);
721:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, false);
722: 
723:       /* Power off the Touch Panel */
724: 
725:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power);
726:       priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
727:     }
728: 
729:   /* Set the Reference Count */
730: 
731:   priv->cref = use_count;
732: 
733:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
734: 
735:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
736:   return OK;
737: }
738: 
739: /****************************************************************************
740:  * Name: gt9xx_poll
741:  *
742:  * Description:
743:  *   Setup or teardown a poll for the Touch Panel Device.
744:  *
745:  * Input Parameters:
746:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
747:  *   fds   - The structure describing the events to be monitored, OR NULL if
748:  *           this is a request to stop monitoring events.
749:  *   setup - true: Setup the poll; false: Teardown the poll
750:  *
751:  * Returned Value:
752:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
753:  *
754:  ****************************************************************************/
755: 
756: static int gt9xx_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
757:                       bool setup)
758: {
759:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
760:   FAR struct inode *inode;
761:   bool pending;
762:   int ret = 0;
763:   int i;
764: 
765:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
766: 
767:   iinfo("setup=%d\n", setup);
768:   DEBUGASSERT(fds);
769:   inode = filep->f_inode;
770:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
771:   priv = inode->i_private;
772: 
773:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Poll Waiters */
774: 
775:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
776:   if (ret < 0)
777:     {
778:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
779:       return ret;
780:     }
781: 
782:   if (setup)
783:     {
784:       /* If Poll Setup: Ignore waits that do not include POLLIN */
785: 
786:       if ((fds->events & POLLIN) == 0)
787:         {
788:           ret = -EDEADLK;
789:           goto out;
790:         }
791: 
792:       /* Find an available slot for the Poll Waiter */
793: 
794:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS; i++)
795:         {
796:           /* Found an available slot */
797: 
798:           if (!priv->fds[i])
799:             {
800:               /* Bind the poll structure and this slot */
801: 
802:               priv->fds[i] = fds;
803:               fds->priv = &priv->fds[i];
804:               break;
805:             }
806:         }
807: 
808:       if (i >= CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS)
809:         {
810:           /* No slots available */
811: 
812:           fds->priv = NULL;
813:           ret = -EBUSY;
814:         }
815:       else
816:         {
817:           /* If Interrupt Pending is set, notify the Poll Waiters */
818: 
819:           pending = priv->int_pending;
820:           if (pending)
821:             {
822:               poll_notify(&fds, 1, POLLIN);
823:             }
824:         }
825:     }
826:   else if (fds->priv)
827:     {
828:       /* If Poll Teardown: Remove the poll setup */
829: 
830:       FAR struct pollfd **slot = (FAR struct pollfd **)fds->priv;
831:       DEBUGASSERT(slot != NULL);
832: 
833:       *slot = NULL;
834:       fds->priv = NULL;
835:     }
836: 
837:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Poll Waiters */
838: 
839: out:
840:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
841:   return ret;
842: }
843: 
844: /****************************************************************************
845:  * Name: gt9xx_isr_handler
846:  *
847:  * Description:
848:  *   Interrupt Handler for Touch Panel.
849:  *
850:  * Input Parameters:
851:  *   irq     - IRQ Number
852:  *   context - IRQ Context
853:  *   arg     - Touch Panel Device
854:  *
855:  * Returned Value:
856:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
857:  *
858:  ****************************************************************************/
859: 
860: static int gt9xx_isr_handler(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
861: {
862:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *)arg;
863:   irqstate_t flags;
864: 
865:   DEBUGASSERT(priv);
866: 
867:   /* Begin Critical Section */
868: 
869:   flags = enter_critical_section();
870: 
871:   /* Set the Interrupt Pending Flag */
872: 
873:   priv->int_pending = true;
874: 
875:   /* End Critical Section */
876: 
877:   leave_critical_section(flags);
878: 
879:   /* Notify the Poll Waiters */
880: 
881:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
882:   return OK;
883: }
884: 
885: /****************************************************************************
886:  * Public Functions
887:  ****************************************************************************/
888: 
889: /****************************************************************************
890:  * Name: gt9xx_register
891:  *
892:  * Description:
893:  *   Register the driver for Goodix GT9XX Touch Panel.  Attach the
894:  *   Interrupt Handler for the Touch Panel and disable Touch Interrupts.
895:  *
896:  * Input Parameters:
897:  *   devpath      - Device Path (e.g. "/dev/input0")
898:  *   dev          - I2C Bus
899:  *   i2c_devaddr  - I2C Address of Touch Panel
900:  *   board_config - Callback for Board-Specific Operations
901:  *
902:  * Returned Value:
903:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
904:  *
905:  ****************************************************************************/
906: 
907: int gt9xx_register(FAR const char *devpath,
908:                    FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c_dev,
909:                    uint8_t i2c_devaddr,
910:                    const struct gt9xx_board_s *board_config)
911: {
912:   struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
913:   int ret = 0;
914: 
915:   iinfo("devpath=%s, i2c_devaddr=%d\n", devpath, i2c_devaddr);
916:   DEBUGASSERT(devpath != NULL && i2c_dev != NULL && board_config != NULL);
917: 
918:   /* Allocate the Touch Panel Device Structure */
919: 
920:   priv = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct gt9xx_dev_s));
921:   if (!priv)
922:     {
923:       ierr("GT9XX Memory Allocation failed\n");
924:       return -ENOMEM;
925:     }
926: 
927:   /* Setup the Touch Panel Device Structure */
928: 
929:   priv->addr = i2c_devaddr;
930:   priv->i2c = i2c_dev;
931:   priv->board = board_config;
932:   nxmutex_init(&priv->devlock);
933: 
934:   /* Register the Touch Input Driver */
935: 
936:   ret = register_driver(devpath, &g_gt9xx_fileops, 0666, priv);
937:   if (ret < 0)
938:     {
939:       nxmutex_destroy(&priv->devlock);
940:       kmm_free(priv);
941:       ierr("GT9XX Registration failed: %d\n", ret);
942:       return ret;
943:     }
944: 
945:   /* Attach the Interrupt Handler */
946: 
947:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_attach);
948:   priv->board->irq_attach(priv->board, gt9xx_isr_handler, priv);
949: 
950:   /* Disable Touch Panel Interrupts */
951: 
952:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
953:   priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, false);
954: 
955:   iinfo("GT9XX Touch Panel registered\n");
956:   return OK;
957: }
